docs.title: About Unimined
docs.text: Welcome to Unimined, a unified Minecraft modding environment supporting modern and legacy Minecraft alike — one Gradle plugin suite covering everything from alpha-era jar mods to current releases.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified environment DSL — minecraft { } binds a source set to a version, loaders, and mappings; multiple environments per project or across modules.
  • Whole-history loader coverage — alpha through current releases, across the forge, fabric, and bukkit families (see below).
  • Configurable remap pipeline — remap { } step specs produce the production-namespace jar (remapJar), remapped dependencies, and sources jars.
  • Production runs — runProdClient/runProdServer launch your mod against the Minecraft artifact it will actually link to at ship time.
  • Mod metadata generation — mod { } emits fabric.mod.json, mods.toml, manifest attributes, and more, era-correct per loader.
  • Project init CLI — unimined init scaffolds ready-made mod projects (see unimined-cli).
  • Adapters — JvmDowngrader, Stonecutter, ExpectPlatform, Forgix, PatchBase, and ModPublisher integrate as unimined.adapter-* plugins.

docs.title: Supported Loaders
docs.text:
• Fabric, Quilt, LegacyFabric, Ornithe, and Babric — the whole intermediary family, alpha to current
  • Forge — merged-jar FG1 era (≤1.6.4), userdev FG2 era (1.7.10–1.12.2), and modern installer-era, including LexForge and Cleanroom
  • NeoForge — userdev-era and 26.x unobfuscated
  • Rift, LiteLoader, ModLoader (Risugami), and plain jar-modding via JarModAgent
  • Craftbukkit/Spigot and Paper
  • Vanilla conversions — ReIndev, NSSS, Better-Than-Adventure, FoxLoader
  • Merged multi-loader environments — repeat loader() in one env; the first declaration is primary (see Multiple Source Sets & Projects)

• Sponge
  • NilLoader
  • ~~Flint Loader~~ (removed — maven.flintloader.net offline; reintroducible if the host returns)

docs.title: Custom Loaders
docs.text: you can create a custom patching/transforming process for minecraft, for example PrcraftExampleMod's buildsrc dir — or register a loader descriptor, see Loaders.

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x to 2.0
docs.text: Unimined 2.0 splits the monolithic unimined { } extension into per-domain plugins with their own extensions. Groovy scripts that call removed 1.x verbs now get a migration note naming the new form; Kotlin DSL scripts fail at compile time — this table maps old calls to their 2.0 equivalents.

docs.title: What's new in 2.0
docs.text:
Not just moves — the rewrite lands a wave of loader-parity features you'll hit while porting (each links to its guide page):

Environments & products

  • Compile-time client split — splitEnvironmentSourceSets() turns main into a common (client∩server) compile env and binds an aux client env; client runs redirect automatically (Environments).
  • Merged multi-loader envs — repeat loader(name, version) in one env: the first is the primary (prod/remap/runs), the rest are compile-classpath secondaries — the 1.x merged { } analog (Multi-project).
  • Declared-source dists — legacydist { file/maven/url/producer } for jars with no manifest provider; bta/reindev/nsss/custom dist presets on unimined { } or any env (Products).
  • Dev bundles — devbundle { file(...) } consumes paperweight zips; devBundleExport { } + export<Env>DevBundle produces a self-contained bundle of the env's prod artifact (Products).

Aux envs & mod groups

  • datagen() / gametest() — auxiliary source-set envs that inherit the parent's sections; datagen materializes a run<Data> config, gametest wires the loader's JUnit artifact + test task (Datagen, Gametests).
  • mods { } classpath groups — name which source-set outputs make up each mod on a dev launch; serializes onto fabric.classPathGroups / MOD_CLASSES, subset via run.loadedMods (Environments).

Runs

  • runProdClient/runProdServer — launch the prod-namespace artifact + remapped jar (1.x runObf* parity) (Run configs).
  • Launch scripts — genLaunchScript<Name>/genLaunchScripts write runnable run<Name>.sh/.cmd into the run dir (Run configs).
  • uniminedRuns report — one line per declared run (task, env, side, type, main class) (Run configs); plus -Punimined.run.dryRun to print an assembled launch without exec'ing.
  • Run surface fill-out — systemProperties, logLevel/ loggingConfigFile, additionalRuntimeClasspath + the run<Name>Dependencies bucket, type (bind a run to a loader's data/junit/gameTestServer launch shape), unitTest + test<Name> JUnit twins, from() run inheritance, ideName/ ideFolderName/ideConfigGenerated, singleInstance (IDEA singleton configs) (Run configs).

Mappings, remap & access

  • UML-backed mapping pipeline — one mappings { } chain per env; channels span yarn/yarnv1, quilt, mcp, retroMCP, searge, mojmap, feather/calamus/legacyIntermediary/ babricIntermediary, legacyYarn/barn/biny/nostalgia, unknownThingy, and Ornithe enrichers (nests/sparrow/raven, auto-contributed on Ornithe envs), parchment, spigot, forgeBuiltinMCP, inline stubs, and the builtin(name) escape hatch (Mappings).
  • hierarchyNameFill — tri-state bytecode hierarchy fill that propagates mapped member names to unmapped overrides (auto-on with Ornithe enrichers); customIntermediaries suppresses loader-contributed intermediary hops — both live on mappings { } as Property<Boolean>s: .set(true) in Kotlin, = true still works in Groovy (Mappings).
  • remap { } step pipeline — typed step specs per surface (remap, remapAccess, modArtifacts, plus engine verbs unpick/nester/raven/sparrow/condor/preen, jst, sourceRemap, applyClassTweaker, downgrade, expectPlatform); remappedViews remaps arbitrary dependency buckets (Remap pipeline).
  • Unified access { } DSL — semantic AW/AT/CT declarations (accessible/extendable/mutable + transitive-* twins, injectInterface, extendEnum, at, file from(...), fileName/format/validate) emitted in the loader's consumed format; validate<Env>Access checks declared targets without a remap (Environments).

Packaging & tooling

  • mod { } metadata — era-correct emitters per loader (fabric.mod.json, quilt.mod.json, mods.toml, mcmod.info, manifest attrs); include nested jars in fabric or jarjar layout with fmlModType marking and deterministic recompress (Mod Metadata, Dependencies).
  • uniminedTools { } — override the build-time tool coordinates (JST, unprotect, mcpcleanup, DiffPatch, jvmdg, classpath-plugin-loader, stitch) (Dependencies).
  • Repo management — loader mavens auto-register per env; uniminedRepos.<name>.ensure() adds a known repo by name, and a post-DSL diagnostic warns on missing/misordered repos (Dependencies).
  • Sources & IDE — gen<Env>Sources/gen<Env>ModSources (external engines via source { generator(dep) }), opt-in cleanup<Env>Sources decompile-cleanup fixups, genIdeRuns/gen<Env>IdeaRuns/gen<Env>EclipseRuns with stable argfile indirection, and pruneUniminedCache for the shared cache (Sources, Run configs).
  • enabled convention — toggles are Property<Boolean>s with an env > inherited > global > default precedence; runs { enabled.set(false) } disables every run task, per-run enabled gates one — new opt-outs follow this pattern (the legacy disableLvtPatch()/disablePreen()/disableNests() verbs stay for compat).

docs.title: Environment configuration
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 unimined.minecraft(sourceSet) { } unimined.minecraft { } + per-source-set env (minecraft { sourceSet("main") { } }) unimined.reIndev(sourceSet) { } unimined.minecraft { reindev { } } (dist preset on main) or per-env sourceSet("x") { reindev { } } unimined.bta(sourceSet) { } unimined.minecraft { bta { } } or per-env bta { } — same for nsss { }/custom("name") { }

Loader declaration moves onto the environment. Every 1.x env.<patcher> { } block — fabric, quilt, forge/ minecraftForge, neoForge/neoForged/neoforge, cleanroom, legacyFabric, babric, ornitheFabric/ornithe, jarMod, foxLoader, liteloader, rift, spigot, paper, bukkit/craftBukkit — is now loader("<id>", "<version>") (bukkit/craftBukkit → loader("craftbukkit", …)). The jar-mod era keeps dedicated verbs too: env.jarmod("x") / env.fg1("x") / env.customSearge().

Special cases:

  • merged { fabric; forge } — gone as a block; repeat loader(...) in one env instead. The first declaration is the primary (owns prod namespace, remap, metadata, runs); later ones are compile-only secondaries (Multi-project).
  • modloader/risugami (Risugami's ModLoader) — ModLoader is not a loader in 2.0; it's a jar-mod dependency. Declare jarmod("<agentVersion>") (or loader("jarmod", …)) and put jarMod("risugami:modloader:<mcVersion>") on the env — the jarmod-modloader-fixes step patches ModLoader.class in dev automatically. loader("modloader")/loader("risugami") fail with unknown loader.
  • nil (NilLoader), folia, arch — no 2.0 loader descriptor exists yet; loader("<id>") for these fails with unknown loader. NilLoader is on the planned list.
  • flint { } — removed entirely: maven.flintloader.net is offline so net.flintloader:* artifacts are unresolvable. The descriptor can return via LoaderRegistry + a mirrored repo if the host comes back.

Kept verbatim on the environment: customGameProvider (suppresses the loader's built-in MC game-provider lookup for total-conversion setups — emits the descriptor's skipMcProvider system property; typically paired with an empty-* version, which still parses as a resolve-nothing pseudo-version).

Other env-level 1.x forms:

1.x 2.0 env.accessWidener(path) / env.accessTransformer(path) access { from("path") }, or the accessWideners/accessTransformers file collections (accessWideners.from(...)) env.version "1.20.1" / env.side "joined" (call form) version = "1.20.1" / version.set(...); side = Side.MERGED / side.set(...) — both are Propertys now (Groovy = assignment still bridges, incl. joined/combined → MERGED) env.runs { } nested inside an env runs { } is top level (runs { } / unimined.runs { }), not per-env env.source { } / env.generator(dep) nested inside an env unimined.source { generator(dep) } — decompile-engine config is global env.remap(...) / env.remapSources(...) task verbs auto-wired remap<Env>Jar / remap<Env>SourcesJar production tasks; custom artifact remaps go through unimined.remap { } surfaces env.obfuscated = true read-only now — env.obfuscated is a Provider<Boolean> the provider resolves (unobfuscated MC builds come back false); do not assign env.defaultRemapJar = false kept as Property<Boolean> — env.defaultRemapJar.set(false) disables the auto remap<Env>Jar/prod-sources wiring (Groovy = assignment is rejected — .set only) env.defaultRemapSourcesJar / env.createJarTask gone — defaultRemapJar gates the whole prod jar+sources wiring; there is no per-artifact opt-out env.canCombine removed — merge semantics are fixed; declare merges via combineWith/from env.useUnionRelaunch / env.onMergeFail removed — no equivalents provider internals (mcPatcher, minecraftRemapper, tinyRemapperConf, minecraftData, minecraftDependency, minecraftFileDev, minecraftSourceFileDev, mergedOfficialMinecraftFile, forgeMCVersion, isMinecraftJar, combinedWithList, localCache) removed — no DSL equivalent

docs.title: Remap pipeline
docs.text: 1.x 2.0 remap hooks inside unimined { } unimined.remap { } — step verbs (unpick(...), applyClassTweaker {}, sourceRemap {}) per surface, both Groovy and Kotlin. Source remapping runs through UML's source remapper by default; jst {} remains as an explicit engine opt-in (verification/alternate engine), not a peer default unimined.migrateMappings(sourceSet) { } unimined.migrateMappings("main") { } (env id), or unimined.migrate { } surface devNamespace/prodNamespace/devFallbackNamespace namespaces come from the environment's declarations — devNamespace, devRemapSourceNamespace, modSourceNamespaces on the env, plus the remap { } step's output remapAccessWidener / remapAccessTransformer / remapATToLegacy remapAccess { } step on the surface tiny-remapper callbacks — config, tinyRemapperConf, remapper(TinyRemapper.Builder), addResourceRemapper, addExtension engine knobs live on the remap { }/engine step specs (jsr305ToJetbrains covers replaceJSRWithJetbrains, on by default) allowImplicitWildcards removed — no equivalent; open an issue if a workflow depended on it

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
The ~25 unimined.*Maven()/unimined.*Repos() helpers (fabricMaven, minecraftForgeMaven, curseMaven, jitpack, spigot, quiltMaven, ornitheMaven, legacyFabricMaven, neoForgedMaven, cleanroomRepos, modrinthMaven, glassLauncherMaven, parchmentMaven, babricMaven, …) are gone: loader repositories are auto-registered per environment in 2.0. Remove the calls; use a normal repositories {} block for anything custom. modsRemapRepo is likewise managed internally.

If a script just wanted to ensure a known repo by name, the uniminedRepos catalog does it (uniminedRepos.fabric.ensure()); a post-DSL diagnostic warns when an ensured repo goes missing or Mojang Libraries ends up ahead of MavenRepo (Dependencies).

docs.title: Other moves
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 mod/transform config inside unimined { } unimined.mod { }, unimined.transform { } (unimined.mods { } → top-level mod { }) global toolchain toggle unimined.useToolchains = false env java override unimined.javaVersion (delegates to the main env) jvmArgs += "-javaagent:/path/agent.jar" javaagents.from(file("agent.jar")) on the run config — a typed file collection resolved to -javaagent: flags at launch

Unknown or removed verbs raise a GradleException naming the replacement — read the message; it points here. Verbs contributed by optional plugins (jarmod, patchBase, jvmdowngrader, devBundleExport, transform, remap engine steps) name the plugin to apply when it isn't.

docs.title: Task names
docs.text:
2.0 standardizes per-environment tasks on verb<Env>Noun — the env id sits between the verb and the object, and the main environment drops it (genSources, remapJar, validateAccess). Every renamed task keeps its old name as a deprecated alias that warns and delegates, so existing scripts/CI keep working:

pre-convention name canonical name applySourcePatch<Env>, createSourcePatch<Env>, createClassPatch<Env> apply<Env>SourcePatch, create<Env>SourcePatch, create<Env>ClassPatch recompileMc<Env>[Classes] recompile<Env>Mc[Classes] forgeSources<Env> gen<Env>ForgeSources genIdeaRuns<Env>, genEclipseRuns<Env> gen<Env>IdeaRuns, gen<Env>EclipseRuns generate[Env]ModMetadata gen[Env]ModMetadata migrateMappings<Env> migrate<Env>Mappings exportMappings<Env> export<Env>Mappings exportMainDevBundle, downgradeMainClasses, validateMainAccess, … exportDevBundle, downgradeClasses, validateAccess — main drops the infix

docs.title: Declared-source provider (legacydist)
docs.text:
New in 2.0: environments whose game jar has no manifest-backed provider declare the artifact directly instead of shipping a bespoke provider — BTA/ReIndev-style jars, pre-1.8 bukkit, offline/air-gapped artifacts:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        main.legacydist {
            file("libs/bta-7.3-client.jar") // or maven("g:a:v"),
            // url("https://...", sha256 = "..."),
            // producer("./tool", "dist", output = "out.jar")
            namespace = "official"          // jar's prod namespace
            format = "obf"  // optional — raw->dev remap view
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        main.legacydist {
            file("libs/bta-7.3-client.jar") // or maven("g:a:v"),
            // url("https://...", "..."),
            // producer("./tool", ["dist"] as String[], [], "out.jar")
            namespace = "official"          // jar's prod namespace
            format = "obf"  // optional — raw->dev remap view
        }
    }
}

legacydist {} selects provider("legacydist") implicitly (apply xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.legacydist to register it); the jar is cached by descriptor and reported with the declared namespace/format. URLs are pinned by SHA-256 (warned-but-allowed when omitted); maven coordinates resolve at declaration time; producer() runs its declared executable inside the artifact transform and requires the artifact's output path (Groovy passes the vararg slot as an explicit String[] — see the example). A format naming a registered provider (e.g. "devbundle") routes there instead; devbundle { } and the bta/reindev/nsss/custom presets accept the same source verbs.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 runs.off global kill-switch unimined.runs { enabled.set(false) } — disables every generated run task; enabled also exists per run config preLaunch(name) { } / preLaunch(name, task) beforeRun { } / beforeRun(task) on the run config, or tasks.named("prepareRun<Name>") { } runs.configFirst(name) { } kept — runs { configFirst(name) { } } applies ahead of named/create/configureEach config (declare it before other configuration of the run) RunConfig.setProperty(key, closure) ${key} substitution kept — setProperty(key, value) (String / Provider / () -> String / Groovy closure, all lazy) and the launchProperties map; ${key} substitutes across jvmArgs/programArgs/systemProperties/environmentVariables at launch, winning over env defaults and loader keys runObfClient/runObfServer runs prodClient/prodServer run configs (runProdClient/runProdServer tasks) — the prod flag launches the prod-namespace artifact

New-in-2.0 run knobs you'll meet while porting — type (bind a run to a loader's data/junit/gameTestServer launch shape), unitTest/unitTestSources (JUnit test<Name> twins), loadedMods (mods { } group subset), systemProperties, logLevel/loggingConfigFile, additionalRuntimeClasspath + the run<Name>Dependencies bucket, stdin, features, width/height, downloadAssets, ideName/ideFolderName/ ideConfigGenerated/singleInstance, from() run inheritance — all documented in Run configs.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: unimined.auth.enabled is gone. 2.0 uses per-run auth { } blocks, with runs { auth { } } as the shared default; with no auth {} declared the run launches offline. A run declaring auth { microsoft() } with an empty credential store fails fast instead of prompting mid-launch — authenticate once via the loginMicrosoft task or a stored token (see Auth).

docs.title: Mappings
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 stubs { } / hasStubs() inline stub rows (c/f/m) mappings { stubs("official", "named") { } } — same c/f/m row verbs against declared namespaces, composes through the normal pipeline and participates in the mapping cache key yarnv1(build) tiny-v1 yarn mappings { yarnv1("build") } — restored, still stitch-filled ExportMappingsTask unimined.exportMappings("<envId>") { } — registers export<Env>Mappings, writing the resolved env tree to a file in a chosen format spigotDev(mcVersion) mappings { spigot() } (or builtin("spigot")) — resolves the BuildData archive for the env's MC version mixinRemap { off(); disableRefmap(keys) } remap { <surface> { modArtifacts { off() / disableRefmap(...) } } } — auto-gating on jar markers still applies; these are the manual overrides customIntermediaries plain var Property<Boolean> on mappings { } — customIntermediaries.set(true) in Kotlin, customIntermediaries = true still works in Groovy AccessConvert.aw2at/at2aw/mergeAws helpers internal — declared accessWidener/accessTransformer files (or access { } rules) are converted to the loader's canonical format automatically during processResources

hierarchyNameFill is new rather than moved — a Property<Boolean> tri-state (unset auto-enables with Ornithe enricher sources) that fills unmapped overrides from the real class hierarchy; see Mappings.

docs.title: Source generation
docs.text:
1.x 2.0 generator("g:a:v") arbitrary decompiler dep unimined.source { generator("g:a:v") } — a bare version string still resolves to org.vineflower:vineflower:<v>; sets engine = "external" + dependency jvmArgs, javaVersion, args same names on unimined.source { }; engine, dependency, options also exposed directly

The external engine wraps any Fernflower-CLI-compatible artifact; vineflower remains the default builtin.

docs.title: Removed extension points (SPI breaking changes)
docs.text:
1.x exposed implementation callbacks that 2.0 replaces with the step-spec pipeline. There is no direct port — write a *StepSpec or transformer claim instead:

  • customPatcher, mcPatcher, minecraftRemapper, remapper(TinyRemapper.Builder), tinyRemapperConf, addResourceRemapper, addExtension, config, replaceJSRWithJetbrains → remap step specs on each remap { } surface (jsr305ToJetbrains for the last).
  • onMergeFail, canCombine overrides → fixed merge semantics — declare merges via combineWith/from; merge configuration knobs are stripBundledServerLibraries, mergeExcludeGlobs, mergeIncludeGlobs on the env.
  • defaultRemapSourcesJar, createJarTask, isMinecraftJar, minecraftDependency, forgeMCVersion, useUnionRelaunch, mods.remap(arbitraryConfiguration), getClasspathAs, catchAWNamespaceAssertion, loader(dep) arbitrary-notation overload, obfuscated, combinedWithList, localCache, minecraftData, minecraftFileDev, minecraftSourceFileDev, mergedOfficialMinecraftFile → no equivalent; open an issue if a workflow depended on one. (defaultRemapJar does survive as an env Property<Boolean> — env.defaultRemapJar.set(false) — the sources-jar twin does not.)
  • -Dfabric.remapClasspathFile / classPathGroups / intermediaryClasspath → deliberate redesign: mod dependencies arrive pre-remapped through mods handling; no system-property seam. Classpath-embedded mods built against a foreign namespace are not detected or runtime-remapped — they are remapped as-if at modSourceNamespaces and fail at runtime; set the env's modSourceNamespaces or use remap.remappedViews(...). The classpath-grouping half does have an equivalent — declare per-mod source-set groups in the env's mods { } container and select them per run with loadedMods (serializes onto fabric.classPathGroups/MOD_CLASSES; see Environments).

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
Adapters are opt-in Gradle plugins that bridge third-party tools into Unimined. They live in unimined-adapters/ and publish as xyz.wagyourtail.unimined:adapter-<tool>.

They share a common shape:

  • Opt-in — applying an adapter without its target tool is a no-op (or a logged warning); they activate via withPlugin when the tool's plugin is present.
  • Stable plugin ids — adapter coordinates may move between artifacts, but plugins {} ids do not change.
  • Environment-scoped — most adapters hang their DSL off each sourceSet("...")/environment block.
Adapter Plugin id Bridges Java JvmDowngrader xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.jvmdg JvmDowngrader bytecode downgrade 17+ ModPublisher xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher ModPublisher uploads 17+ PatchBase xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase PatchBase patch sets 17+ Forgix xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix Forgix loader-jar merge 17+ Stonecutter xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter Stonecutter version envs 21+ ExpectPlatform xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-expectplatform ExpectPlatform agent 17+ Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined")
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase") version "2.0.0"
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined'
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase' version '2.0.0'
}

docs.title: Upstream versions
docs.text:
Adapters couple to their tools in three ways — each has its own knob for running a newer upstream release than the one Unimined shipped against, so a minor upstream update rarely requires a Unimined update:

Coupling How it works Version knob Detected plugin adapter hooks withPlugin(id) and reads the upstream extension when you apply it bump the version in your own plugins {} block — the adapter detects whatever you resolve Resolved artifact engine/tool jars resolved from a named configuration at execution override the coordinate on uniminedTools, or declare a dependency on the adapter's configuration directly In-process engine engine classes linked on the adapter's classpath Gradle dependency substitution on the plugin classpath — bounded by binary compatibility of the entry points the adapter calls

Per-adapter defaults and overrides:

Adapter Bundled default How to override Forgix uniminedTools.forgix → io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.0.0 uniminedTools { forgix.set("...:2.1.0") } or a loaderMergeForgix dep — resolved into an isolated classloader, so the override is the merge implementation JvmDowngrader uniminedTools.jvmdowngraderJavaApi → jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.0.1 uniminedTools { jvmdowngraderJavaApi.set("...:2.1.0") } for the stub jar; engine bumps via applying xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader yourself or classpath substitution PatchBase none — patch-set coords are yours version lives in the patchBase("g:a:v") declaration Stonecutter none — adapter detects plugins { id("dev.kikugie.stonecutter") version "..." } ExpectPlatform none — adapter detects plugins { id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.expect-platform") version "..." } ModPublisher none — adapter detects plugins { id("com.hypherionmc.modutils.modpublisher") version "..." }

Where an adapter resolves its engine reflectively through an isolated classloader (currently just Forgix's mergeLoaders), a bumped coordinate is all that's needed — incompatible versions fail the task with a clear error naming the missing entry point rather than a NoSuchMethodError.

Kotlin build.gradle.kts — overriding a tool coordinateGroovy build.gradle — overriding a tool coordinateKotlin build.gradle.kts — classpath substitution escape hatch 
uniminedTools {
    forgix.set("io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0")
}

uniminedTools {
    forgix.set('io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0')
}

// settings.gradle.kts (or a buildscript block)
configurations.classpath {
    resolutionStrategy.dependencySubstitution {
        substitute(module("io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix"))
            .using(module("io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0"))
    }
}

docs.title: ExpectPlatform adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-expectplatform

Bridges ExpectPlatform into Unimined. ExpectPlatform's own insertAgent(JavaExecSpec) can't attach to Unimined runs (they aren't JavaExecSpecs), and dev-vs-prod needs different handling — the adapter covers both:

  • Dev runs get the javaagent + -Dexpect.* sysprops, including -Dexpect.side so the agent strips the other side's @Environment-annotated members at classload (dev classes are raw; loaders scan bytes before transforms — issue #4)
  • The prod jar gets ExpectPlatform's transform applied statically as a JAR-surface step — @ExpectPlatform redirects, @PlatformOnly filtering, and annotation remaps are resolved into the artifact, so runProd* runs and shipped jars need no agent
  • modImplementation/modRuntimeOnly are marked for ExpectPlatform's artifact transform, so resolved mod jars (e.g. a shared common module) arrive already platform-transformed

Requires both xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.expect-platform and xyz.wagyourtail.unimined applied — the adapter activates when both are present.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
The canonical multi-loader setup — the @ExpectPlatform stub lives in the shared env, one <pkg>/<platform>/<Class>Impl class per loader env:

my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/
    ├── main/java/com/example/
    │   └── Platform.java              # @ExpectPlatform stubs
    ├── fabric/java/com/example/fabric/
    │   └── PlatformImpl.java          # real impl for "fabric"
    └── forge/java/com/example/forge/
        └── PlatformImpl.java          # real impl for "forge"

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
Code
docs.text:
// src/main/java/com/example/Platform.java — shared env
public final class Platform {

    // Body is replaced at transform time by
    // com/example/<platform>/PlatformImpl.loaderName()
    @ExpectPlatform
    public static String loaderName() {
        throw new AssertionError();
    }

    // Present only on the listed platforms — filtered out elsewhere
    @PlatformOnly("forge")
    public static void forgeOnlyThing() {}
}

// src/fabric/java/com/example/fabric/PlatformImpl.java
public final class PlatformImpl {
    public static String loaderName() { return "fabric"; }
}

// src/forge/java/com/example/forge/PlatformImpl.java
public final class PlatformImpl {
    public static String loaderName() { return "forge"; }
}

@Environment(EnvType.CLIENT) marks side-only members with ExpectPlatform's own annotation — in the prod jar it is remapped to the loader's side annotation (see the table below), and in dev the agent strips the other side's members at classload.

docs.title: Per-env knobs
docs.text:
platform(name, remap) sets platformName/remap on the env's expectPlatform extension and marks its mod-dep configurations. All of it resolves lazily — a common env's platform(...) propagates to combineWith children by convention, and each knob is per-env overridable:

Property Default Purpose enabled true master switch — off: no agent, no jar step agent true off: drop the javaagent + sysprops from runs, keep the static jar transform platformName inherited the ExpectPlatform platform name remap table + inherited + explicit annotation-descriptor remaps (see below) stripAnnotations false strip ExpectPlatform's own annotations from output

docs.title: The @Environment remap table is filled for you
docs.text:
remap defaults to a built-in table for the env's platform — the same maps ExpectPlatform's README documents:

  • fabric (and legacyfabric/babric/ornithe) → net.fabricmc.api.Environment/EnvType
  • quilt → org.quiltmc.loader.api.minecraft.MinecraftOnlyIn/EnvType
  • forge → era-picked by env.version: ≥1.13 net.minecraftforge.api.distmarker.OnlyIn/Dist, 1.8–1.12 net.minecraftforge.fml.relauncher.SideOnly/Side, ≤1.7.10 cpw.mods.fml.relauncher.SideOnly/Side
  • neoforge → net.neoforged.api.distmarker.OnlyIn/Dist
  • cleanroom → the 1.12-era fml table

Explicit remap entries merge over the table (table < inherited env < explicit). Loaders with no side-annotation convention (vanilla, jarmod, modloader, bukkit family) get none.

docs.title: Manual jar step
docs.text:
The same static transform is declared as a JAR-surface verb when you want it on a specific product instead of env-wide:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
jar {
    expectPlatform { platformName.set("fabric") }
}

jar {
    expectPlatform { platformName.set("fabric") }
}

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 17+
  • xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.expect-platform ≥ 1.2.0 for side stripping; the agent jar resolves from the applied plugin's version — bump it in your plugins {} block, the adapter detects it via withPlugin

docs.title: Forgix (loader-jar merge)
docs.text: Adapter plugin xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix (adapter-forgix) merges per-loader production jars with Forgix's engine (Forgix.mergeLoaders) and publishes the result on the consumable mergedElements configuration (classifier merged).

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/
    ├── main/         # common env
    ├── fabric/       # fabric env → remapFabricJar
    └── forge/        # forge env → remapForgeJar

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
Inputs
docs.text:
Three sources feed the merge, in increasing precedence:

  1. Bound environments — auto-injected. Every non-auxiliary env's production jar (remap<Env>Jar, or the env's plain jar), keyed by loaderSpec.name (env id as fallback; same-loader collisions become <name>-<envId>). Needs no configuration.
  2. forgix { } DSL — optional. When io.github.pacifistmc.forgix is also applied, entries in forgix.mergeConfigurations feed in (explicit inputJar wins; the subproject heuristic is the fallback). On flat projects, write them via the map — upstream's merge(name) validates before running its action and always throws for non-subproject names.
  3. loaderMerge.from(...) — optional override. Only needed for extra inputs or key collisions — the env feed already covers the standard case:
Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
uniminedLoaderMerge {
    from(
        "quilt" to tasks.named("remapQuiltJar").flatMap { it.archiveFile },
    )
}

uniminedLoaderMerge {
    from {
        input("quilt", tasks.named("remapQuiltJar").flatMap { it.archiveFile })
    }
}

Inputs may be Files, task references, or providers — task-output providers carry their producer, so inputs always build before the merge runs.

docs.title: Engine version
docs.text:
The adapter does not link Forgix from its own classpath — mergeLoaderJars resolves it from the loaderMergeForgix configuration and invokes Forgix.mergeLoaders through an isolated classloader, so the coordinate you set is literally the merge implementation that runs.

  • Bundled default: io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.0.0 (the version the release was tested against)
  • Override — coordinate: set uniminedTools.forgix:
Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
uniminedTools {
    forgix.set("io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0")
}

uniminedTools {
    forgix.set('io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0')
}
  • Override — direct dependency (useful for forks, local jars, or a different repository artifact): declaring anything on loaderMergeForgix replaces the default entirely:
Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
dependencies {
    loaderMergeForgix("io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0")
    // or loaderMergeForgix(files("libs/Forgix-custom.jar"))
}

dependencies {
    loaderMergeForgix 'io.github.pacifistmc.forgix:Forgix:2.1.0'
}

The only contract is Forgix.mergeLoaders(Map, File) — an incompatible version fails the task with an explicit "does not expose mergeLoaders" error rather than a NoSuchMethodError.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text: adapter-modpublisher prefers the mergedElements artifact as the upload artifact automatically — and suppresses the per-loader jars — so applying all three plugins means a merged multi-loader jar is what gets published.

docs.title: JvmDowngrader adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.jvmdg

Bridges JvmDowngrader into Unimined so environments targeting ancient JVMs (Java 8 and below-era loaders) can compile on a modern JDK while producing downgraded bytecode for dev runs, production jars, and api jars.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/main/

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
source and target
docs.text:
Two separate levels, because downgrading decouples them:

Setting Meaning Default source Java level compile* tasks run at — toolchain selection, --release, sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility, Kotlin jvmTarget the env's Java requirement (era floor or javaVersion) target class-file level JvmDowngrader emits, as a major (8 → v52) the env's Minecraft Java floor — the version-json javaVersion, floored at 7 for ≤1.6.4-era

source raises the compile level only — run launchers and tool executions still use the env's Java requirement, so a 1.7.10 env with source.set(21) compiles on a Java 21 toolchain while FML still launches on Java 8. Unset, the env compiles at its requirement and the downgrade passes through untouched.

target is a convention, not a fixed value — most projects leave it alone and get the era floor. To override:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
jvmdowngrader {
    source.set(21)
    target.set(11) // emit v55 instead of the era floor
}

jvmdowngrader {
    source.set(21)
    target.set(11)
}

jvmdowngrader(N) remains as shorthand for jvmdowngrader { target.set(N) }.

docs.title: Toolchains
docs.text: With minecraft.useToolchains on (the default), source selects the Java toolchain for compile* independently of the run JVM — e.g. a Java 21 toolchain compiles while the run still launches on the era JVM. With toolchains off, the build JVM itself must meet source — a 1.7.10 env with source.set(21) requires running Gradle on Java 21+, and fails with a clear diagnostic otherwise.

docs.title: What gets downgraded
docs.text:
Once enabled and source exceeds target:

  • dev runs — run* tasks launch against JvmDowngrader-processed copies of classesDirs plus downgraded api jars, so era loaders whose bundled ASM can't read modern class files (FG-era LaunchWrapper/FML reads ≤v52; ≤1.6.4-era reads ≤v51) run modern-compiled mods
  • production — the same downgrade is contributed to the env's production jar pipeline, so runProd and published artifacts carry era-readable bytecode instead of raw javac output. It applies to the env's own jar only — the Minecraft artifact and remapped dependency views are untouched
  • api — jvmdowngrader-java-api stubs are shaded into an api-*.jar next to the outputs so emitted classes resolve their xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdg.jdk.stub.* references at runtime

For ad-hoc jars outside the env pipeline, remap { downgrade(8) } still applies the step directly to any remap surface.

docs.title: Engine flags
docs.text: Both specs implement JvmDowngrader's Gradle ShadeFlags, so the engine's own knobs are settable on either block — globally or per env — and flow to both the dev-class and prod-jar downgrades: downgradeTo (engine-level emit level; a direct set wins over target), apiJar, ignoreWarningsIn, logLevel, multiReleaseVersions, shadeInlining, quiet, and the debug* switches. See JvmDowngrader's DowngradeFlags docs for the full list.

docs.title: Upstream versions
docs.text:
Two pieces carry versions — they override independently.

java-api stub jar — bundled default xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader:jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.0.1, resolved per-environment from uniminedTools.jvmdowngraderJavaApi. Bump it to pick up newer stub coverage (e.g. a newer Java major's VersionProviders) without a Unimined release:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
uniminedTools {
    jvmdowngraderJavaApi.set(
        "xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader:jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.1.0")
}

uniminedTools {
    jvmdowngraderJavaApi.set(
        'xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader:jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.1.0')
}

A direct jvmdgJavaApi<Env> dependency also works and replaces the default for that environment.

Engine + global flags — the engine stays on the adapter's classpath at the bundled version, but applying JvmDowngrader's own Gradle plugin (xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader) alongside this adapter does two things: its jvmdg { } extension is detected and becomes the deepest global flag layer (env set > inherited > minecraft { jvmdowngrader { } } > jvmdg { } > built-in default), and your plugins {} version wins classpath conflict resolution — effectively bumping the engine the adapter links against:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader") version "2.1.0"
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader' version '2.1.0'
}

For an engine bump without applying upstream, use the classpath substitution shown in upstream versions.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 17+ to run the build (the adapter itself targets 17)
  • Consumes xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader:jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.0.1 directly (overridable via uniminedTools.jvmdowngraderJavaApi)
  • Old-forge dev runs require this when your compile target is newer than Java 8

docs.title: ModPublisher adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher

Feeds your build's production artifacts + metadata into ModPublisher's own publisher { } DSL as conventions — the adapter owns selection and plumbing only; ModPublisher's engine is applied by you. There is no adapter DSL: publisher { } stays the single surface for what can't be inferred, and anything you set there always wins.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── build.gradle.kts
└── src/
    ├── main/         # common env → common prod jar
    ├── fabric/       # fabric env → remapFabricJar
    └── forge/        # forge env → remapForgeJar

docs.title: build.gradle.kts
What conventions in
docs.text:
publisher field Convention artifact the forgix mergedElements jar when adapter-forgix is applied, else the first bound env's production jar (remap<Env>Jar when it remaps, else jar) additionalFiles the remaining per-loader prod jars loaders bound envs' loaderSpec.names gameVersions bound envs' versions version project.version

Selection: the merged artifact wins when present and suppresses the per-loader jars; aux envs (gametest/datagen) are excluded; dev jars are never selectable.

docs.text:
• Java 17+

docs.title: PatchBase adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase

Bridges PatchBase patch sets into Unimined environments. Two flows:

  • Authoring a patch set against Minecraft (a "patchbase modloader" project — the git repo carries only patch files)
  • Consuming patch sets — modding against an MC jar mutated by .binpatch/.bdiff entries, the same seam Forge binpatches occupy

The adapter consumes the standalone patchbase artifact (xyz.wagyourtail.unimined:patchbase:2.0.0) — PatchBase's core has no Unimined dependency; this plugin is only the env bridge.

docs.title: Project layout (authoring)
docs.text:
my-patchbase/
├── build.gradle.kts
├── patches/            # git-tracked unified diffs — the repo's
│                       #   only real content
└── src/main/java/      # generated patched sources — gitignore this

docs.title: build.gradle.kts (authoring)
Consuming patch sets
Authoring a patch set
Notes
docs.text:
• Patch sets bind to a base jar. .binpatch/.bdiff entries carry a checksum of the class they were built against — create patch jars against the env's pre-remap base (minecraftRaw), which is what createClassPatch uses, or consumers' checksums won't match
  • The dev flow mirrors Forge binpatches: the patch jar mutates the MC jar, so the loader's classes exist for compile and runtime without loader sources or a recompile
  • The patch-set version lives in the patchBase("g:a:v") coordinate you declare on the env — there is no bundled default to override

docs.title: Stonecutter adapter
docs.text:
Plugin id: xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter

Bridges Stonecutter into Unimined for multi-version projects. When dev.kikugie.stonecutter is applied, every Unimined environment's version conventions to the chiseled project's version (stonecutter.current.version) — so the shared build script doesn't repeat version = stonecutter.current.version in every target. An explicit version on an environment always wins.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
my-mod/
├── settings.gradle.kts      # stonecutter plugin + version tree
├── build.gradle.kts         # central script — applied to every
│                            #   chiseled version project
├── gradle.properties
├── src/main/                # shared sources (java/kotlin/resources)
└── versions/
    ├── 1.20.4/
    │   └── gradle.properties  # per-version dep versions
    └── 1.21.1/
        └── gradle.properties

docs.title: settings.gradle.kts
build.gradle.kts (central script)
docs.text:
Applied to every version project — the adapter supplies env.version from the chiseled version, so this script stays version-free:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "..."
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter") version "..."
    kotlin("jvm") version "..."
}

group = "com.example.mymod"

unimined {
    minecraft {
        // env.version conventions to stonecutter.current.version —
        // "1.20.4" when building that project, "1.21.1" for the other
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
    }
}

dependencies {
    // per-version dep versions come from each version's
    // gradle.properties — stonecutter exposes them as `deps.*`
    // project properties
    modImplementation("net.fabricmc:fabric-loader:${property("deps.fabric_loader")}")
    modImplementation("net.fabricmc.fabric-api:fabric-api:${property("deps.fabric_api")}")
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined' version '...'
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-stonecutter' version '...'
    id 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm' version '...' // TODO-groovy: kotlin plugin alias
}

group = "com.example.mymod"

unimined {
    minecraft {
        // env.version conventions to stonecutter.current.version —
        // "1.20.4" when building that project, "1.21.1" for the other
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
    }
}

dependencies {
    // per-version dep versions come from each version's
    // gradle.properties — stonecutter exposes them as `deps.*`
    // project properties
    modImplementation("net.fabricmc:fabric-loader:${property("deps.fabric_loader")}")
    modImplementation("net.fabricmc.fabric-api:fabric-api:${property("deps.fabric_api")}")
}

docs.title: versions/1.20.4/gradle.properties
docs.text:
deps.fabric_loader=0.16.9
deps.fabric_api=0.102.0+1.20.4

Per-version build-script overrides are also possible (versions/<ver>/build.gradle.kts); the shared script still wins only where it doesn't set explicit values.

docs.title: Multi-loader envs
docs.text:
Stonecutter wires sourceSets.all { }, so Unimined's env-per- source-set model works per version project — each env's sources get the same shared + version-specific layering and chisel comment processing as main:

my-mod/
└── src/
    ├── main/                # shared across loaders and versions
    ├── fabric/              # fabric env sources
    └── forge/               # forge env sources
versions/1.20.4/
└── src/
    ├── main/                # version-specific overrides
    └── forge/               # per-version, per-loader overrides
Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
// central build.gradle.kts
unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")            // main env

        sourceSet("forge") {
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")         // forge env — also
        }                                     //   chiseled per version
    }
}

// central build.gradle
unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")            // main env

        sourceSet("forge") {
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")         // forge env — also
        }                                     //   chiseled per version
    }
}

Each version project then produces jar + remapFabricJar + remapForgeJar for its own version — the full version×loader matrix inside one chiseled project. Ordering is safe: sourceSets.all is a live callback, so envs created after Stonecutter's plugin is applied are still picked up. This composes with adapter-expectplatform, adapter-forgix (merges that version's loader jars), and adapter-modpublisher.

Upstream Stonecutter templates sometimes encode the loader in the version id instead (versions("1.20.4-fabric")) — that also works but gives one project per loader×version pair; the per-source-set layout above keeps all loaders for a version in one project.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 21 — Stonecutter publishes Java-21 bytecode, so the adapter module targets 21 too (the rest of Unimined stays at 17)
  • dev.kikugie.stonecutter must be applied; without it the adapter logs a warning and does nothing
  • The Stonecutter version is whatever you put in your plugins {} block — the adapter detects it via withPlugin, so bump it there without waiting on Unimined

docs.title: unimined-cli
docs.text:
unimined generates complete modding environments — the single entry point for new projects. Binaries ship per-platform (native .kexe, fat jar, Node build).

unimined new mymod --group com.example --version 1.20.1 --loader fabric=0.16.0

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Unimined 2.0 is a Gradle plugin. Your settings.gradle.kts carries three pieces:

  • pluginManagement.repositories — where Gradle resolves the plugin itself (the maven.wagyourtail.xyz repos + gradlePluginPortal()). Required.
  • dependencyResolutionManagement.repositories — settings-level dependency repos applied to every project that doesn't declare its own repositories { } (the generated module scripts do declare theirs, so this is a fallback).   • includeBuild("…") — optional, local composite development only (resolves the plugin from a source checkout instead of a maven artifact). Drop it for normal use.

pluginManagement {
    repositories {

        maven("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/releases/")
        maven("https://maven.wagyourtail.xyz/snapshots/")
        mavenCentral()
        gradlePluginPortal()
    }
}

dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        mavenLocal()
        mavenCentral()

    }
}

rootProject.name = "examplemod"
