Then apply the plugin in build.gradle.kts:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined") version "2.0.0-SNAPSHOT"
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined' version '2.0.0-SNAPSHOT'
}

The frontend applies the java plugin for you — source sets, compile tasks, and the IDE model are wired without declaring it. (The lower-level xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.* plugins stay Java-agnostic on purpose; if you apply them individually instead of the frontend, declare java yourself or environments stay inert and a warning is logged.)

Skip the typing

unimined-cli new mymod --group com.example --version 1.20.1 --loader fabric=0.16.0 emits this whole structure for you — see unimined-cli.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Run configurations carry a typed auth { } spec — each run decides how its session is produced. 2.0 has no project-global runs.auth: per-run, provider-backed, and nothing token-shaped ever lands on the configuration model or in the config cache.

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    runs {
        named("client") {
            auth { microsoft() }
        }
        named("server") {
            auth { offline("DevServer") }
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    runs {
        named("client") {
            auth { microsoft() }
        }
        named("server") {
            auth { offline("DevServer") }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Verbs
docs.text:
Verb Session produced offline(name) Offline-mode session — deterministic UUID from the player name (default) microsoft() Microsoft account — stored credential + silent refresh custom(provider) Any AuthProvider — the extension point for third-party auth (Ely.by, launchers) injected(prefix) Session read from UNIMINED_AUTH_* env vars at execution — the CI path

username = "x" on a run is the back-compat shorthand for auth { offline("x") } — an explicit auth spec wins over it.

docs.title: A default for every run
docs.text:
runs { auth { } } configures the default applied to all runs — per-run auth/username values always win:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    runs {
        auth { microsoft() }         // everything logs in...
        named("server") {
            auth { offline("Srv") }  // ...except the server
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    runs {
        auth { microsoft() }         // everything logs in...
        named("server") {
            auth { offline("Srv") }  // ...except the server
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Microsoft login
docs.text:
Run loginMicrosoft once on a machine with a browser — it prints the device-code URL + code, completes the MSA → Xbox → Minecraft chain, and stores the credential. Runs then consume the store with a silent refresh; they never prompt mid-launch — a missing credential fails fast with the remediation in the message.

Store: <unimined global cache>/auth/credentials.json, written 0600, one serialized session per username.

docs.title: Gradle properties
docs.text: Property Default Purpose unimined.auth.username — Account selector for loginMicrosoft and for microsoft() runs when more than one user is stored unimined.auth.encrypt false Opt-in AES-256-encrypted store, key from the OS keyring via java-keyring (loaded reflectively — add com.github.javakeyring:java-keyring to the build classpath). No plaintext fallback: encrypt on + no keyring = explicit failure unimined.auth.storeCredentials true false reads+refreshes stored credentials in memory only — nothing is written back

docs.title: CI / headless
Notes
docs.text:
• Sessions materialize inside the run task's execution — access tokens never appear in task inputs, the config cache, or logs.
  • auth { injected() } never writes to the credential store.
  • Old single-player-era launchers passed session details as user_properties — the resolver still substitutes it; Microsoft sessions leave it empty.

docs.title: Datagen
docs.text:
env.datagen() declares an auxiliary environment for data generation — separate sources, its own classpath, but sharing the parent env's Minecraft/loader/mappings via implicit-parent inheritance:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        datagen()                          // env "data" → runData
        // or: datagen(client = true)      // client-side pack
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version.set("1.20.1")
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        datagen()                          // env "data" → runData
        // or: datagen("data", true)       // client-side pack
    }
}

docs.title: What it wires
docs.text:
• src/data/ (or src/<env>Data/) — your datagen entrypoints live here, compiled against the parent's classpath
  • src/<parent>/generated is added to the parent env's resources — generated JSON/tags/recipes land in the mod jar automatically
  • A run<Data> configuration materializes from the loader's datagenMain/datagenArgs capabilities — {output} in the arg template resolves to src/<env>/generated
  • client = true appends the loader's datagenClientArg (fabric: --client) for client-side packs

The mod still declares its loader's datagen entrypoint itself (e.g. fabric's fabric-datagen key in fabric.mod.json) — unimined only provides the env, classpath, and run.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: datagen() defaults to data on main, <env>Data elsewhere; datagen("mygen") overrides. It's an aux env (isAuxEnv) — excluded from publication and loader-jar merging.

docs.title: Loaders without datagen
docs.text: If the loader descriptor has no datagenMain capability, the run still registers but launches the plain game — a warning is logged. Forge supplies datagenArgs through its userdev capabilities; older loaders need a manual runs.named("data") { mainClass = … }.

docs.title: Mod dependencies (artifacts)
docs.text:
Each env exposes mod* configurations scoped to its source set — mod jars land remapped onto your mappings:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
dependencies {
    modImplementation("maven:coord")
    modCompileOnly("maven:coord")
    modLocalRuntime("maven:coord")
}

dependencies {
    modImplementation("maven:coord")
    modCompileOnly("maven:coord")
    modLocalRuntime("maven:coord")
}

Mod jars are remapped from the environment's mod source namespace to its dev namespace — they must already be built against the mod source namespace (usually the loader's production namespace, e.g. intermediary on Fabric). A jar built against any other namespace is remapped as if it were at the declared one and breaks at runtime — there is no per-jar namespace sniffing (the 1.x remapClasspathFile/classPathGroups runtime-remap machinery is gone by design). If your mod set mixes namespaces, set the env's modSourceNamespaces to match or declare per-namespace remap.remappedViews(...) and wire the buckets yourself.

Whether a jar remaps at all is decided by a marker scan of its contents (mod metadata, namespace attributes, MC references); plain libraries pass through. Metadata reads are qmj5-tolerant — a quilt.mod.json written in JSON5 (comments, trailing commas, bare keys) parses the same as strict JSON, both in dependency jars and in your own resources. Loom's manifest contract is honored — Fabric-Loom-Remap: false opts a jar out even when markers exist, true forces remap of an unmarked jar. The user-side escape is forceRemap { dep -> … } on the environment (NeoGradle's forceDeobfuscation equivalent) — predicates select components that must remap regardless of markers:

unimined.minecraft {
    sourceSet("main") {
        // …
        forceRemap { it.group == "com.example" && it.name == "obf-lib" }
    }
}

forceRemap also accepts a group:name[:version] coordinate string (forceRemap("com.example:obf-lib")); malformed notation fails the build with an actionable error.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
Loader environments auto-register the mavens their artifacts resolve from (Mojang Libraries, the loader's own maven, and friends) — no repositories { } entries are needed for unimined-managed coordinates. Your own repos still go through the normal repositories { } block, and the uniminedRepos catalog can ensure a known repo by name (uniminedRepos.fabric.ensure()).

After the build script evaluates, unimined runs repository diagnostics automatically — the FG7 checkRepos equivalent, but as post-DSL validation, not a task you invoke. The checks are warn-only and land in the Gradle problems report (unimined/repo-missing, unimined/repo-order) as well as the console:

  • every repo unimined ensured earlier is still present — a repo removed or renamed mid-configuration is flagged;
  • MavenRepo (Maven Central) must precede Mojang Libraries — module artifacts pin to the repo that served their metadata, so a mojang-first order hides central-only classifiers (e.g. netty natives).

A dependencyResolutionManagement.repositoriesMode build is honored rather than bypassed: a repo already declared in settings satisfies the ensure, FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS without one fails with the settings block to paste, and PREFER_SETTINGS reports a problem and skips the project-level registration.

docs.title: Jar-in-jar (include)
docs.text:
Each env exposes an include configuration (<env>Include for named source sets). Artifacts declared there are embedded inside the production jar and declared in its loader metadata:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
dependencies {
    include("maven:coord")
    include(files("libs/local.jar"))
}

dependencies {
    include("maven:coord")
    include(files("libs/local.jar"))
}

include is an ordinary declarable configuration, so bulk composition rides extendsFrom rather than a dedicated option — e.g. configurations { include extendsFrom(embedThese) } embeds everything declared on a custom bucket. Inherited deps still produce version.range metadata entries, so platform-include-style grouping needs no extra DSL.

Two formats, chosen per environment — normally by the loader claim (fabric-family → fabric, forge → jarjar) or explicitly:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    transform {
        sourceSet("main") {
            features { nestedJars("jarjar") } // or "fabric"
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    transform {
        sourceSet("main") {
            features { nestedJars("jarjar") } // or "fabric"
        }
    }
}

The transform knobs can also sit directly on the loader declaration — loader(name, version) { } receives the same environment's transform spec (nestedJars { } plus binding(key, value) for feature bindings), so packaging config colocates with the loader it belongs to:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("forge", "47.2.0") {
            nestedJars { recompress.set(false) }
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("forge", "47.2.0") {
            nestedJars { recompress.set(false) }
        }
    }
}

Both paths write the same spec — pick whichever reads better; loader(name) { } works too for loaders that resolve their own version. The env-scoped transform { } verb reaches the same spec directly (minecraft { transform { nestedJars { } } } for main, or inside sourceSet("x") { } for named environments).

  • fabric — jars pack under META-INF/jars/ and the loader metadata key (jars in fabric.mod.json, quilt_loader.jars in quilt.mod.json) gains {file} rows. Nested jars missing loader metadata get a synthesized stub so the loader accepts them.
  • jarjar — jars pack under META-INF/jarjar/ (STORED — forge's runtime byte-range-reads them) plus META-INF/jarjar/metadata.json rows in the net.neoforged.jarjar schema (identifier, version range/artifactVersion, path, isObfuscated). File dependencies without Maven coordinates fall back to Automatic-Module-Name / Implementation-Version manifest attributes.

docs.title: Entry type marking (jarjar)
docs.text:
FML classifies every discovered jar by the FMLModType manifest attribute — MOD, LIBRARY, GAMELIBRARY (nested-jar default), LANGPROVIDER, CUSTOM — which also picks its JPMS layer: LIBRARY/LANGPROVIDER land in the PLUGIN layer (visible to language providers), MOD/GAMELIBRARY in GAME. Stamping it is how you mark a nested jar for FML's mod pipeline (scan, runtime remap) without mods.toml inside it:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    transform {
        sourceSet("main") {
            nestedJars {
                fmlModType.set("LIBRARY") // default for every entry
                fmlModTypes.put(
                    "com.example:lang-lib", "LANGPROVIDER") // per g:a
                fmlModTypes.put("local.jar", "MOD") // per file name
                obfuscated.put("com.example:obf-lib", true)
            }
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    transform {
        sourceSet("main") {
            nestedJars {
                fmlModType.set("LIBRARY") // default for every entry
                fmlModTypes.put(
                    "com.example:lang-lib", "LANGPROVIDER") // per g:a
                fmlModTypes.put("local.jar", "MOD") // per file name
                obfuscated.put("com.example:obf-lib", true)
            }
        }
    }
}

Unset entries aren't blindly left alone — during the rewrite pass the embedder resolves layer signals in order:

Signal Stamps Why the jar's own FMLModType manifest attribute keeps it the author knows its layer — outranks every heuristic META-INF/services/…​IModLanguageProvider (or IModLanguageLoader) LANGPROVIDER providers must be PLUGIN-layer — the Kotlin-for-Forge case META-INF/mods.toml / neoforge.mods.toml MOD it is a mod file Obfuscated-By manifest attribute GAMELIBRARY needs game-layer runtime remap parent jar's FMLModType is LIBRARY/LANGPROVIDER/CUSTOM LIBRARY plugin-layer parents propagate to their deps — FML does the same at runtime post-1.20

Explicit config always wins over everything, including a shipped FMLModType; LIBRARY is never auto-detected (nothing inside a jar proves it doesn't touch game classes) beyond the parent-propagation rule. With no signal at all the jar embeds unstamped — FML's GAMELIBRARY default applies, which can't break anything since GAME sees PLUGIN.

Detection only rides the rewrite pass: recompress.set(false) embeds verbatim with no stamp unless you declare a type explicitly — which still forces the rewrite (the manifest is emitted first so JarFile sees it). isObfuscated otherwise detects from the nested jar's own Obfuscated-By manifest attribute.

include is not a classpath dependency — declare modImplementation (fabric-style mods) or implementation (jarjar library deps) alongside when dev runs need the contents.

docs.title: Recompression
docs.text:
By default embedded jars are rewritten before packing: entries sorted and stamped at a fixed epoch for reproducible builds, STORED for fabric so the outer jar compresses the whole nested stream once (verbatim embedding would double-compress for ~zero gain). Opt out per environment:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    transform {
        sourceSet("main") {
            nestedJars { recompress.set(false) } // embed verbatim
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    transform {
        sourceSet("main") {
            nestedJars { recompress.set(false) } // embed verbatim
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Identity environments
docs.text:
Environments with no dev→prod namespace remap (identity envs — e.g. unobfuscated targets, or devNamespace == modSourceNamespaces) skip remapJar entirely. The embed runs as a post-pass on the plain jar task there instead, so include behaves identically whether or not a remap hop exists.

Nested jars stamped with a different Unimined-Mapping-Namespace than the production target produce a warning — embed the production-namespace artifact.

docs.title: Loader apis
docs.text:
unimined.loaderApi(name, version) resolves a loader's api artifact bundle; loaderApiModule(name, module, version) resolves one sub-module. Both also record the api modid into mod { depends }.

## loaderApi providers

docs.title: Metadata-only dependencies
docs.text: mod { depend("modid", "versionRange") } declares runtime deps in the emitted mod metadata without touching the classpath.

docs.title: Tool coordinates
docs.text:
Unimined resolves several build-time tools into detached configurations — JST (source-transform enrichment), unprotect (forge dev launches), mcpcleanup/DiffPatch (mcpconfig pipelines), the jvmdowngrader java-api, the bukkit classpath-plugin-loader, and stitch (yarn-v1 field-name proposals). Each coordinate is a Property<String> on the uniminedTools extension, so the version — or a fork — is user-overridable:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
uniminedTools {
    jst.set("net.neoforged.jst:jst-cli:2.1.0")
    diffpatch.set("com.example:DiffPatchFork:1.0")
}

uniminedTools {
    jst.set("net.neoforged.jst:jst-cli:2.1.0")
    diffpatch.set("com.example:DiffPatchFork:1.0")
}

Available keys and defaults:

Key Default coordinate Used for jst net.neoforged.jst:jst-cli:2.0.11 Forge userdev source-pipeline enrichment unprotect io.github.juuxel:unprotect:1.3.0 Forge-era dev launches mcpcleanup net.minecraftforge:mcpcleanup:2.3.6 Notch-obf userdev sources chain diffpatch net.minecraftforge:DiffPatch:2.0.12 MCPConfig diff/patch steps jvmdowngraderJavaApi xyz.wagyourtail.jvmdowngrader:jvmdowngrader-java-api:2.0.1 jvmdg adapter runtime dep classpathPluginLoader xyz.wagyourtail.unimined:classpath-plugin-loader:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT:all Bukkit plugin-classpath agent stitch net.fabricmc:stitch:0.6.2 yarn-v1 proposeFieldNames

Overrides match by the default group:artifact — wherever the default tool coordinate appears (including inside mcpconfig functions tables and userdev tool lists) the overridden notation is substituted. Coordinates a loader profile itself declares stay profile-driven unless their group:artifact matches a key above.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
An environment is a Minecraft instance bound to a source set — the unit that owns a product, loaders, mappings, run configs, and mod* dependency configurations.

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        // bound to main by default
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        // or a named source-set env:
        sourceSet("server") {
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
            side = Side.SERVER
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        // bound to main by default
        version.set("1.20.1")
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        // or a named source-set env:
        sourceSet("server") {
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
            side.set(Side.SERVER)
        }
    }
}
  • sourceSet(name) binds the env to a source set (default main); sibling envs are independent — combineWith("other") (optionally with EnvironmentSections) composes one into another, and nested envs (datagen()/gametest()) inherit their parent implicitly.
  • side selects Side.CLIENT/SERVER/MERGED (example / groovy); Side.COMMON is applied by splitEnvironmentSourceSets() (below).
  • Multiple envs in one project = flat multi-env; multi-module is the alternative.

Envs are also the scope of mod { } metadata and runs { }.

Task naming. Per-environment tasks follow verb<Env>Noun — the environment id (capitalized) sits between the verb and the object: genFabricSources, validateForgeAccess, remapClientJar, exportPaperDevBundle. The main environment elides the infix: genSources, validateAccess, remapJar. Task names normalized onto this convention keep their old shape as a deprecated alias — gradlew oldName warns and runs the canonical task.

docs.title: Environment knobs
docs.text:
Everything below lives inside an env block (minecraft { … } or sourceSet("x") { … }):

  • Java — javaVersion sets the compile/run floor (conventioned from the loader descriptor); useToolchains toggles Gradle toolchains for env-scoped compiles (conventioned from the extension-level unimined.useToolchains); requiredJavaVersion reads the effective requirement — version-json javaVersion raised by your javaVersion — and feeds launchers and tool-exec fallbacks. compileJavaVersion is the level compile* tasks actually emit at (toolchain selection, --release, sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility, Kotlin jvmTarget) — it conventions to requiredJavaVersion, and the jvmdg adapter's source raises it without moving the run floor.
  • Access widening — accessWideners / accessTransformers are file collections of *.accesswidener / accesstransformer.cfg applied to the dev artifact; transitiveAccessWideners (default true) lets AW transitive-* directives from compile-classpath mods contribute — set false to isolate the dev jar. dependencyInterfaceInjection (default true, loom's interfaceInjection.enableDependencyInterfaceInjection) controls dependency-declared *injected_interfaces independently — mods injecting interfaces you compile against still apply when transitiveAccessWideners is off. The access { } block below covers inline rules, file declarations, and resource auto-discovery.
  • Prod packaging — defaultRemapJar (default true) auto-wires remap<JarTask> so the jar task's input gains a -dev classifier and the remap task produces the prod-namespace artifact; apiOnly tells bukkit-family transforms to compile against the loader's api artifact instead of building the patched server jar.
  • Merge controls — stripBundledServerLibraries (default true) drops pre-1.13 server-jar entries that duplicate minecraftLibraries jars during the client+server merge; mergeExcludeGlobs adds entry globs to strip; mergeIncludeGlobs marks entries that are never stripped.
  • Library resolution — manifestUrls adds ordered version-manifest locations searched after Mojang's; libraryOverlays merges {name, url?, maxGameVersion?} overlay lists into the version JSON; librarySubstitutions / replaceLibraryVersion(group, name, classifier) { … } rewrite matched library versions (regexes, null drops the library); libraryFilter { dep -> … } keeps a library only when every filter accepts it; libraryCoordFilters maps whole coords; obfuscatedLibraries flags coords that remap with the MC jar.
  • LWJGL 3 swap — lwjgl3 { } drops every org.lwjgl.lwjgl:* library (jars and natives entries) and puts lwjgl3 artifacts on the classpath and the host natives set instead — the RetroFuturaGradle surface for running old Minecraft on modern JVMs:
Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
minecraft {
    sourceSet("main") {
        version = "1.7.10"
        lwjgl3 {
            version.set("3.3.3")
            bindings.add("stb")           // + natives
            nativeslessBindings.add("harfbuzz")
        }
    }
}

minecraft {
    sourceSet("main") {
        version.set("1.7.10")
        lwjgl3 {
            version = "3.3.3"
            bindings.add("stb")
            nativeslessBindings.add("harfbuzz")
        }
    }
}

Natives resolve under the host's lwjgl3 classifier (natives-windows/natives-linux/natives-macos + -x86/-arm64 variants). The lwjgl3ify mod itself — for environments needing the lwjgl2 API at runtime — is a normal modImplementation/include dependency; this block only swaps the bindings. - Ornithe artifact passes — loader("ornithe", …) environments get Ploceus's default-on Minecraft-jar passes automatically: condor synthesizes LocalVariableTable debug info on the dev artifact (versions before 1.8.2 — every alpha/beta build plus releases and snapshots up to 1.8.2-pre*; infdev and older stay out) so decompilers and Mixin @Local captures see real variable slots, and preen splits ProGuard-merged bridge methods back into ACC_BRIDGE delegates on every Ornithe version. The newest net.ornithemc:nests build published for the env's version + side also joins the mapping chain automatically (see Mappings). Each pass opts out individually:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
minecraft {
    sourceSet("main") {
        version = "b1.7.3"
        loader("ornithe", "0.19.5")
        disableLvtPatch()   // skip the condor LVT pass
        disablePreen()      // skip the bridge-method pass
        disableNests()      // skip the auto nests source
    }
}

minecraft {
    sourceSet("main") {
        version.set("b1.7.3")
        loader("ornithe", "0.19.5")
        disableLvtPatch()
        disablePreen()
        disableNests()
    }
}

The passes scope to the environment artifact — remapped dependency views and remapJar outputs never see them. patchLvts, applyPreen and autoNests are the underlying booleans behind the disable* verbs. - combinedSources / combinedOutputs — file collections populated by combineWith; read-mostly, used by generated source jars and mod packaging.

docs.title: Split environment source sets
docs.text:
Loom splitEnvironmentSourceSets() parity — compile-time client/server separation on a single project:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        splitEnvironmentSourceSets()
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version.set("1.20.1")
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")
        splitEnvironmentSourceSets()
    }
}

src/main compiles against the common artifact — the intersection of the client and server jars (Side.COMMON) — so shared code can't reference client-only classes (Minecraft, screens, rendering). Client-only code lives in src/client, which compiles against the full client jar and sees main's output (its compile classpath picks up main's classesDirs, its runtime classpath the full output).

  • main → Side.COMMON; the client env (src/client) → Side.CLIENT and aux status — it inherits main's loader/dependency/access sections and produces no separate published artifact or mod metadata of its own.
  • jar folds the client output in, so remapJar/remapSourcesJar carry it through production; sourcesJar gains the client sources; test sees the client's classpath view.
  • runClient/runProdClient — and any client-side run bound to main — launch through the client environment (the common jar can't launch a client); runServer/runProdServer stay on main, where the common jar is the server's view.
  • On providers without genuinely split distributions (declared legacydist jars, dev bundles, BuildTools outputs) the common artifact aliases the merged jar — the client-only fence then only covers entries the shared jar lacks. Non-mergeable conversion products (independent forks like BTA/ReIndev/NSSS) reject COMMON outright — split-source-set mode needs real client+server distributions.
  • The call is idempotent; a pre-existing sourceSet("client") env is repurposed as the split client.

docs.title: Access declarations
docs.text:
Everything in this section is optional — dropping a *.accesswidener, *.classtweaker/.ct, or accesstransformer.cfg/*_at.cfg file under the environment's resource roots is all a file-based setup needs: it's detected, applied to the dev artifact, shipped in the jar, and declared in loader metadata with zero DSL. The access { } block below is for declaring rules inline (no file at all) or attaching packaging options to specific files.

access { } declares every access rule — inline directives, existing files via from(...), and interface injections — stored semantically and emitted in whichever document format the environment's loader consumes (accessWidener/classTweaker on fabric-family, FML accesstransformer.cfg on forge-family). Rules the target format can't express are converted when possible or dropped with a build warning (inject-interface/extend-enum have no AT analog; narrowing at() access has no AW form).

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSets.main {
            access {
                // rename / reformat the merged canonical doc
                // (where the loader declares it in metadata) —
                // here a legacy-FML-style AT at a custom `_at.cfg`
                // path; format: "aw", "at", "legacy_at", default
                // is the loader's consumed format
                fileName = "META-INF/{modid}_at.cfg"
                format = "legacy_at"

                // fail the build when a declared target doesn't
                // exist in the dev artifact — NFRT
                // `--validated-access-transformer` parity; covers
                // every own declaration channel (these rules,
                // from(...) files, accessWideners/
                // accessTransformers). Dependency docs are never
                // validated. Default false.
                validate = true

                // existing files — format detected per file,
                // routed like accessWideners.from(...) /
                // accessTransformers.from(...)
                from("src/main/resources/testmod.accesswidener")

                // per-file packaging options where the loader
                // declares the path — rides the accessFile(...){}
                // channel: `output` ships the file at a custom jar
                // path, `declare=false` applies it dev-side only,
                // `format` forces interpretation when detection
                // can't (e.g. a legacy-AT file with an odd name):
                // "aw"/"accesswidener", "at"/"accesstransformer",
                // "legacy_at"/"legacyat" — classTweaker is
                // detected by its header, not settable
                from("src/main/resources/extra.cfg") {
                    output = "META-INF/extra.cfg"
                    format = "legacy_at"
                }

                // AW directives (+ transitive* twins)
                accessible("net/minecraft/class_123")
                accessible("net/minecraft/class_123", "method_1", "()V")
                extendable("net/minecraft/class_456")
                mutable("net/minecraft/class_456", "field_7", "I")

                // CT directives — interface injection / enum
                // extension (dev jar + shipped CT where the loader
                // parses it)
                injectInterface("net/minecraft/class_123",
                    "com/example/IThing")
                extendEnum("net/minecraft/class_789", "MY_CONST")

                // raw FML AT entries — `at("public-f", "a/B", "f", "I")`
                at("public", "com/example/Opened")
            }
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSets.main {
            access {
                fileName = "META-INF/{modid}_at.cfg"
                format = "legacy_at"
                from("src/main/resources/testmod.accesswidener")
                from("src/main/resources/extra.cfg") {
                    output = "META-INF/extra.cfg"
                }
                accessible("net/minecraft/class_123")
                injectInterface("net/minecraft/class_123",
                    "com/example/IThing")
                at("public", "com/example/Opened")
            }
        }
    }
}
  • Every verb has a transitive* twin (transitiveAccessible, …) matching loom's dependents-visible semantics.
  • interfaceInjection(target, signature) on the env is shorthand for access { transitiveInjectInterface(...) }.
  • Dev artifact — generated declarations and discovered files apply to the dev Minecraft artifact before your sources compile, so widened members and injected interfaces resolve in compileJava.
  • Shipping — the same declarations ride the declared-file channel: they convert into the loader's consumed format at the canonical jar path ({modid}.accesswidener, META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg) and are declared in loader metadata (accessWidener field / FMLAT manifest attribute). On fabric loader ≥ 0.18.0 the canonical doc upgrades to classTweaker when CT rules are present; older loaders get an AW-only doc and interface injections ride the loom:injected_interfaces custom key instead. A loaderless (common) env skips metadata entirely — the canonical doc ships inside the jar instead as a self-describing classTweaker (format also accepts "ct" there), so dependents discover it on their dependency scan and inherit its transitive-* rules.
  • Naming — rules from all access { } calls merge into one canonical doc; fileName = "..." inside the block (or the accessFileName property) renames where that merged doc ships, where the loader's metadata declares the path ({modid} still expands). format = "…" inside the block ("aw"/"at"/ "legacy_at") overrides the emitted format — the default is the loader's consumed format, and overriding warns since the loader parses the declared path in its own expected format. Setting two different names is a configuration error, not two files — for multiple shipped access documents use from(path) { output = "..." }, which emits each named file independently. On loaders with no access-file convention the canonical name is ignored (warn-only).
  • Auto-discovery — resource-side access files (patterns above) join the same channels without any declaration: dev-artifact application, canonical merge, metadata reference.
  • combineWith propagates access rules alongside the declared file collections, so combined environments share declarations.

docs.title: validate<Env>Access
docs.text:
Environments that declare access documents also get a validate<Env>Access task (loom validateAccessWidener parity): every own declaration — access { } rules, from(...) files, accessFile(...), accessWideners/accessTransformers — is checked against the dev Minecraft artifact and the build fails listing each declared target that matched nothing, without running a remap. Dependency docs and coordinate-consumed docs are never validated. check depends on it, so it runs in a normal build; the task only exists when the environment actually declares access docs.

This is the standalone form of access { validate = true } — the in-block flag validates during the remap pipeline instead; either catches stale targets, the task form without needing a remap run.

docs.title: Auto-fill flags
docs.text:
Metadata auto-discovery toggles (see metadata):

Property Default Gates discoverMixinConfigs true *.mixins.json resources auto-fill the mixins array discoverGametestEntrypoints true compiled-class scan for loader gametest interfaces/annotations interfaceInjectionScan false mixin-class scan deriving inject-interface rules (opt-in — access { injectInterface(...) } is the always-on path)

docs.title: Mod classpath groups
docs.text:
Multi-mod projects tell the dev launch which classpath entries belong to which mod via the env-scoped mods { } container — the group name should match the mod id:

minecraft {
    sourceSet("fabric") {
        loader("fabric", "...")
        mods {
            register("mymod") {
                sourceSet("main")
                modFiles("libs/extra-mod-lib.jar")
            }
            register("integration") {
                sourceSet("integration")
            }
        }
    }
}

Each group joins the launch classpath and serializes into the loader's mod-grouping channel:

  • fabric-family — the fabric.classPathGroups system property (fabric-loader's classpath-group contract — loom mods { } parity), groups separated by a doubled path separator;
  • forge-family — id%%dir entries appended to MOD_CLASSES alongside the loader's own source-set groups.

A run loads every declared group by default; loadedMods on the run selects a subset (see run configs). Groups inherit through inheritParent/combineWith like other env state — a child re-declaring a group name shadows the parent's.

docs.title: Minecraft artifact configurations
docs.text:
Each environment registers resolvable configurations producing the Minecraft artifact at each mapping namespace — minecraftRaw, minecraftDev, minecraftProd for main, <env>MinecraftRaw, … for a named env. Resolve them like any configuration — e.g. custom packaging tasks that need the prod artifact read configurations.named("minecraftProd").

Configuration Produces minecraftRaw MC in the source namespace — the artifact the game ships as (obfuscated for obf-era loaders, intermediary for fabric-family, mojmap for unobf'd releases) minecraftDev MC in the dev namespace your sources compile and dev runs launch against minecraftProd MC in the production namespace shipped mod jars are remapped to — the remapJar target. Feeds runProd* classpaths and mod-view remap analysis; collapses to the raw artifact when prod == source namespace minecraftLibraries the MC library set (version-json + loader libraries)

runProd* resolves minecraftProd by default; loaders whose production runtime remaps at launch override the view — FG2-era forge (1.7.10–1.12.2) launches minecraftRaw (the shipped obf jar) and lets FMLDeobfTweaker remap obf→searge at runtime, matching a real installation.

docs.title: Fork Development with Patch Sets
docs.text:
Fork-dev is the mache/git-patch workflow for projects whose real content is a set of edits on Minecraft (or another mod's) decompiled sources — a patchbase modloader, a hacked MC, a heavily patched dependency. The git repo tracks only unified diffs; everything else decompiles and materializes on build.

The workflow lives in the adapter-patchbase plugin — xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-patchbase — which bridges the standalone PatchBase patch tooling onto Unimined environments. It composes two loops:

  • Text patch loop (this page) — patches/ unified diffs over the environment's decompiled sources. This is the mache model: the patch dir is the source of truth, the patched source tree is generated.
  • Class patch loop — the same edits, diffed at the binary level into a shippable .binpatch/.bdiff patch jar that other projects consume via patchBase("g:a:v") — Forge-binpatch-style mutation of the env jar, pre-remap.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
my-fork/
├── build.gradle.kts
├── patches/            # git-tracked: *.java.patch diffs + verbatim
│                       #   *.java for net-new files
└── src/main/java/      # GENERATED patched overlay — gitignore it

# the patch overlay is generated material, not hand-written source
/src/*/java/

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            version.set("1.7.10")
            patchBaseCreator()
        }
    }
}
  1. Materialize — gradlew applySourcePatch runs genSources first (decompile via unimined.source — declare the env, the task exists), then applies patches/ onto the decompiled tree and writes only patch-covered files into src/<env>/java. patches/ absent → the task skips; an empty set produces an empty overlay.
  2. Edit — work in src/<env>/java like a normal source tree. The env compiles it as its own sources; patched classes win over the stock jar at dev runtime through JarModAgent's priority classpath.
  3. Commit — gradlew createSourcePatch diffs src/<env>/java back against the decompiled base and rewrites patches/ — new files copy verbatim, edits become *.patch unified diffs. This is what you commit.
  4. Ship — gradlew createClassPatch diffs the env's production jar (remap<Env>Jar, else the env jar) against its pre-remap base and produces the publishable patch jar (classifier patch). Consumers apply it with patchBase("g:a:v").

Non-main envs put the environment in the middle (applyClientSourcePatch, recompileClientMc, …) and a per-env patch dir (patches/<env>) + overlay (src/<env>/java). The old suffix shape (applySourcePatchClient) still runs as a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Recompiling a patched jar
docs.text:
patchBaseCreator() also wires the FG-era recompMc analog — for when you need the whole patched game as a single artifact, not a patch jar:

recompileMcClasses   compiles the overlay's .java files against the
                     env's dev jar + Minecraft libraries
recompileMc          merges the compiled classes + verbatim resource
                     patches over the dev jar →
                     build/libs/minecraft-<env>-<version>-recompiled.jar

The merge is "first copy wins": the recompiled overlay replaces stock class entries and overlay resources replace stock resources, while unpatched classes, assets and data carry through from the dev jar untouched. The stock manifest and signature blocks are stripped — a jar whose contents changed can't keep Mojang's signatures.

recompileMc reads the overlay as it sits — run applySourcePatch first to regenerate it from patches/ (deliberately not chained: the apply wipes the overlay, and auto-running it on every build would drop uncommitted edits).

What it's for:

  • a local patched install, or a fixture artifact for a downstream environment — legacydist { file("…-recompiled.jar") } with namespace set to the dev namespace the jar carries
  • anything needing the whole patched MC in one file — binpatch bases, dev-bundle inputs, external tooling

What it isn't for:

  • dev runs — the overlay already compiles into the env's own classes and wins on the priority classpath, so runClient sees your patches without a recompiled jar (and makeStart has no analog: run configs launch the dev artifact + libraries directly)
  • shipping to consumers — createClassPatch's binpatch jar is the distribution format (patchBase("g:a:v"))

The overlay is not a source dir

Both applySourcePatch and createSourcePatch delete and repopulate their output tree — treat src/<env>/java as the patch set's checkout, not a place for hand-written sources, or the next apply deletes them. Keep normal mod sources in a separate env or retarget the overlay via the spec below.

docs.title: Customizing the layout
Gametests
docs.text:
env.gametest() declares an auxiliary environment for in-game JUnit tests — real game launches orchestrated per test, not a plain JVM test run:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        gametest()                         // env "gametest"
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version.set("1.20.1")
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        gametest()                         // env "gametest"
    }
}

docs.title: What it wires
docs.text:
• src/gametest/ (or src/<env>Gametest/) — test sources on the parent's classpath via implicit-parent inheritance
  • The loader's gametestJunit coordinate is added to testImplementation ({loader} in the template resolves to the env's loader version — e.g. fabric-loader-junit) and the env's test task is switched to useJUnitPlatform()
  • Client gametests: the gametest env's own <env>GametestClient run gets the loader's gametestClientJvmArgs (-D... flags) — {modid} resolves against mod { id }. Entrypoint classes are declared by the loader (fabric-gametest / fabric-client-gametest keys in fabric.mod.json)
  • Server gametests run inside the JUnit orchestration — no separate run needed

The mod still registers its loader-specific gametest entrypoints — unimined provides the env, classpath, JUnit artifact, and the armed client run.

docs.title: Loaders without gametest support
docs.text:
If the descriptor has no gametestJunit capability the env still compiles (a warning notes the missing artifact) — write your own gametestImplementation coordinate or orchestrate launches via a custom runs.create(...).

Aux env (isAuxEnv) — excluded from publication and merging.

docs.title: Loaders
docs.text:
Each environment declares its loaders inside the env block — loader("<name>", "<version>"). Multi-loader projects either use one env per loader or repeat loader(...) on a single merged env where the extra loaders are compile-only secondaries (merged multi-loader):

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        version = "1.20.1"
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        version.set("1.20.1")
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version.set("1.20.1")
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

Loader names resolve through the loader registry:

## Loader registry
  • Forge is era-aware — loader("forge", …) emits FG1-era wiring on ≤1.7.10, FML-style on 1.8–1.12, and modern Forge ≥1.13 (scripts: 1.7.10, 1.12.2, 1.20.1 — the .gradle siblings are the Groovy twins).
  • Pseudo-loaders — jarmod injects into the MC jar itself (script); --jars split|merged shapes the jar set (split / merged); accessTransformer/accessWidener are transform-only.
  • Products nest loaders — bta { loader("bta-babric", …) }.
  • Single-arg form — inside a named env, loader("0.16.0") reads the lone arg as the version and the env id as the loader name (sourceSet("fabric") { loader("0.16.0") }).
  • Bukkit-family dev plugins — craftbukkit, spigot, and paper stage the dev jar into run/<env>-<run>/plugins/ by default (modDiscovery("plugins")), so the server's own plugin loader discovers it exactly as production does — including plugin.yml/paper-plugin.yml validation and the real plugin classloader (required by JavaPlugin's loader check on Paper). modImplementation plugin deps stage alongside and load for free. Opt back into classpath loading with features { modDiscovery("classpath") } — the ClasspathPluginLoader javaagent then scans source-set output dirs for plugin.yml instead (note: CPL cannot read paper-plugin.yml, so classpath mode only suits plugin.yml-era products).

Loader "api" artifacts resolve via loaderApi — see Dependencies.

docs.title: Adding a loader to an existing project
docs.text:
The manual equivalent of unimined-cli new --loader <name>=<ver>:

  1. Declare the env (a sourceSet env so it doesn't fight the existing main env — or on main for a single-loader project):

=== "Kotlin build.gradle.kts" 

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("quilt") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("quilt", "0.26.0")
        }
    }
}

=== "Groovy build.gradle" 

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("quilt") {
            version.set("1.20.1")
            loader("quilt", "0.26.0")
        }
    }
}

  1. Mappings — the env's mappings { } chain (quilt: quilt(build) named layer — intermediary is contributed automatically; forge: official()/mcp(...)/searge(); see Mappings). Nested envs inherit the main env's declarations — override per env as needed.

  2. Metadata — the env's mod { } block emits the loader's descriptor (fabric.mod.json, META-INF/mods.toml, mcmod.info, …): id, name, version, depends — see Mod Metadata.

  3. Sources — env code lives in src/<env>/ (created with the source set); shared code stays in main — aux/sibling envs inherit the parent's classpath via combineWith or implicit parent inheritance.

  4. Runs — <env>Client/<env>Server register automatically; aux flows use datagen()/gametest() (see Datagen/Gametests).

Generating fresh instead? unimined-cli new mymod --loader quilt=0.26.0 emits the same shape — --modules for the per-loader subproject layout.

docs.title: Mappings
docs.text:
Each env declares a mappings { } chain — the sequence of mapping namespaces the env's MC jar and mod deps get remapped through.

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        mappings {
            yarn(10)              // fabric yarn
            // official()         // mojang official names
            // mcp("stable", "60") // MCP
            // searge()           // srg names
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        mappings {
            yarn(10)              // fabric yarn
            // official()         // mojang official names
            // mcp("stable", "60") // MCP
            // searge()           // srg names
        }
    }
}

Chain order matters — later entries layer onto earlier ones. The full named-mapping catalog lives in the registry; generator-side, --mappings takes the same DSL lines and --var key=val feeds mapping vars (e.g. Ornithe's ornitheGenVersion).

Mod dependencies declared on env mod* configurations are remapped through this chain automatically.

docs.title: Builtin channels
docs.text: Beyond the channels shown above: spigot() (Spigot BuildData mappings — fails loud if the provider can't supply the archive), parchment(mcVersion, version) (Parchment param/javadoc layer), forgeBuiltinMCP(version) (MCP data bundled in FG1 forge :src zips), and yarnv1(build) — Tiny-v1 Yarn for legacy Fabric envs, with stitch proposeFieldNames filled from the client jar.

docs.title: Ornithe enrichers
docs.text:
nests(build) (inner-class attributes), sparrow(build) (generic signatures) and raven(build) (exception mappings) graft net.ornithemc metadata artifacts onto the environment's official columns — split-era merged versions emit one declaration per side. Their elements apply during remap: nests restore InnerClasses attributes for decompilers, signatures and exceptions feed the same metadata path.

On loader("ornithe", …) environments the latest published nests build for the env's version + side is contributed to the chain automatically — the equivalent of Ploceus's always-appended nests mapping layer. An explicit nests(...) declaration wins over the auto-picked build, and disableNests() on the environment opts it out (the contribution also stays inert offline or when the Ornithe meta index is unreachable). The meta base URL is overridable with -Punimined.ornitheMeta=<url> for mirrors or airgapped caches.

docs.title: Stub mappings
docs.text:
stubs declares inline mapping rows when a real channel doesn't cover what you need — values are positional across the namespaces you bind:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
mappings {
    stubs("official", "named") {
        c("a/b", "com/example/Foo") {
            f("a", "someField")
            m("c;()V", "run")
        }
    }
}

mappings {
    stubs(["official", "named"]) {
        c(["a/b", "com/example/Foo"]) {
            f(["a", "someField"])
            m(["c;()V", "run"])
        }
    }
}

Member entries are name[;desc] per namespace; a null cell leaves that namespace unmapped.

Set customIntermediaries on the mappings spec to tell fabric-family loaders your intermediary column is your own, not upstream's — their wiring checks this before contributing net.fabricmc:intermediary:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
mappings {
    customIntermediaries.set(true)
}

mappings {
    customIntermediaries = true
}

docs.title: Bytecode hierarchy fill
docs.text:
hierarchyNameFill scans the environment's raw Minecraft jar plus its runtime libraries for the real class hierarchy, then propagates mapped method and parameter names to overriding declarations the chain leaves unmapped — synthesizing verbatim class/method cells for tree-absent rows so remap does not break references (ploceus MappingFiller parity; this extends the name copying fillMissingNames performs on rows that already exist). The default auto-enables when Ornithe enrichers (nests/sparrow/raven) are declared; true/false forces it:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
mappings {
    feather(4)
    nests(4)
    hierarchyNameFill.set(true) // explicit — unset auto-enables on enrichers
}

mappings {
    feather(4)
    nests(4)
    hierarchyNameFill = true
}

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text: uniminedMinecraft.exportMappings(envId) { } registers an export<Env>Mappings task (exportMappings for main) that writes the env's resolved tree in a chosen format (SRG/TSRG/Tiny/MCP — see ExportMappingsTask for the format + output inputs). The pre-convention exportMappings<Env> name stays as a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Mod Metadata
docs.text:
mod { } inside unimined { } is the mod identity + runtime metadata, emitted into the loader's descriptor (fabric.mod.json, mods.toml, …) at build time:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
minecraft {
        version.set(providers.gradleProperty("minecraft_version"))

        loader("fabric", providers.gradleProperty("fabric_version").get())
        mappings {
            yarn(providers.gradleProperty("yarn_mappings").get())
        }
    }

    mod {
        id.set(providers.gradleProperty("modid"))
        name = "examplemod"
        version.set(providers.gradleProperty("version"))
        loader("fabric") {}

    }
}

dependencies {
    // mods on the classpath — remapped onto your mappings
    // modImplementation("maven:coord")
    // modCompileOnly(...) / modLocalRuntime(...)
    // unimined.loaderApi("fabric", providers.gradleProperty("fabric_api_version").get()) — loader api coords
    // (also records the api modid into mod { depends } automatically)
}

minecraft {
        version.set(providers.gradleProperty("minecraft_version"))

        loader("fabric", providers.gradleProperty("fabric_version").get())
        mappings {
            yarn(providers.gradleProperty("yarn_mappings").get())
        }
    }

    mod {
        id.set(providers.gradleProperty("modid"))
        name.set("examplemod")
        version.set(providers.gradleProperty("version"))
        loader("fabric") {}

    }
}

dependencies {
    // mods on the classpath — remapped onto your mappings
    // modImplementation("maven:coord")
    // modCompileOnly(...) / modLocalRuntime(...)
    // unimined.loaderApi("fabric", providers.gradleProperty("fabric_api_version").get()) — loader api coords
    // (also records the api modid into mod { depends } automatically)
}
  • id, name, version, description, authors, license, url, icon
  • depend(modId, versionRange) — metadata deps
  • loader("fabric") { } / fabric { } — loader-specific sections (entrypoints, extra keys)
  • mixins { create("name") { } } — generated *.mixins.json configs
  • fmlModType("LANGPROVIDER") inside a forge-family loader section — stamps the jar's FMLModType manifest attribute (MOD/LIBRARY/ GAMELIBRARY/LANGPROVIDER/CUSTOM) for jarjar-layer classification; unset leaves FML's own locator discovery in charge

--metadata dsl on the CLI emits this block instead of hardcoding values in the loader descriptor.

docs.title: Loader documents
docs.text:
Each loader family gets its own document shape from the same model:

  • fabric-family → fabric.mod.json (fmj): schemaVersion, top-level id, custom object, loom:injected_interfaces.
  • quilt → quilt.mod.json (real qmj): schema_version, quilt_loader { group, id, version, metadata { name, description, contributors, contact, license, icon }, entrypoints, depends[] }, minecraft.environment (fmj's server value translates to dedicated_server), top-level mixin / access_widener, section custom entries emitted as top-level namespaced keys (qmj's extension convention), interface injections under top-level quilt_loom.injected_interfaces. quilt_loader.group is required by the loader and comes from project.group (unspecified when unset).
  • forge-family → mods.toml / neoforge.mods.toml + manifest attributes per the table below.

docs.title: Merging with hand-written files
docs.text: If a resource already contains the loader's metadata file (e.g. src/fabric/resources/fabric/fabric.mod.json), the generated document is merged into it rather than colliding: objects merge recursively, arrays union and deduplicate, and generated scalar values win. Only the merged copy ships — the source file is excluded from processResources. Non-JSON collisions still fail the build.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
gen<Env>ModMetadata scans the environment's resources and compiled classes at execution time, gated by three env flags:

  • *.mixins.json files found in resources are referenced from the mixins array automatically (generated and hand-written configs union, deduplicated) — discoverMixinConfigs, default true.
  • Classes implementing the loader's gametest interface are added to the fabric-gametest entrypoint; FabricClientGameTest implementors land under fabric-client-gametest — discoverGametestEntrypoints, default true.
  • Mixin classes are scanned for @Mixin targets × implemented interfaces — interfaceInjectionScan, default false (opt-in). Each pair becomes an inject-interface rule: on loaders whose access doc can carry classTweaker directives (fabric ≥ 0.18.0) the rules merge into the canonical *.accesswidener file, and on every loader they emit the loader's injected-interfaces metadata (custom.loom:injected_interfaces on fabric, top-level quilt_loom.injected_interfaces on quilt) for IDE/dependents. Rules already present in the project's own CT/AW files or access { } declarations are not re-emitted.

Interface-injection names are emitted in the dev namespace; the production repack rebases the metadata keys to the published namespace. Dependent projects receive the injections through the dependency-side classTweaker extraction.

Because the scan needs compiled classes, it cannot feed the project's own compile classpath — casts against injected interfaces in first-party sources need a declared rule (access { injectInterface(...) }), which applies to the dev artifact and ships for dependents. The scan only adds dependents-facing metadata.

docs.title: Access files
docs.text:
No DSL is required — an access file under the environment's resource roots (*.accesswidener, *.classtweaker/.ct, accesstransformer.cfg/*_at.cfg) is picked up automatically.

All declared access files — accessWideners/accessTransformers collections, access { } rules, accessFile(...) overrides, and the auto-discovered resource files — convert into the loader's consumed format and merge into one canonical file at the loader's conventional path ({modid}.accesswidener, META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg), which the metadata then declares (accessWidener field, FMLAT manifest attribute). classTweaker documents merge their AW-compatible directives and keep CT-only directives (inject-interface, extend-enum) when the loader version can parse them — fabric ≥ 0.18.0 reads CT content through the accessWidener file — otherwise those directives drop with a warning.

The emitted format is always the env loader's consumed one — conversion is bidirectional, so a modern AT input on an FG1-era env re-emits as legacy *_at.cfg rows, a legacy file on modern forge emits modern at rows, and either emits AW/CT on fabric-family.

Two naming controls exist where the loader's metadata declares the path: the merged canonical doc's jar path is overridable via access { fileName = "…" } / accessFileName ({modid} expands), and individual files carry their own shipped path via accessFile(path) { output = "…" } or access { from(path) { output = "…" } } — declare=false applies a file to the dev artifact without shipping it, and format forces the source interpretation ("aw"/"at"/"legacy_at", plus long names; classTweaker is detected by header only). On loaders with no access-file convention the canonical-name override is ignored (warn-only).

docs.title: Manifest attributes
docs.text:
Manifest-attribute loaders emit a manifest body merged into the env jar via jar.manifest.from(...). The same body also lands in generated resources (META-INF/MANIFEST.MF) so dev runs see it — FML (modern SecureJar and legacy CoreModManager alike) parses manifests inside classpath directories, which is how exploded dev mods carry FMLModType/MixinConfigs/FMLAT. The file copy is excluded from the packed jar; the attrs ride the real manifest.

Environment-fact attributes (Fabric-Mapping-Namespace, MixinConfigs, FMLAT, loader-version stamps, …) describe the environment, not your mod's identity, so they emit even when mod { } is unconfigured — a hand-written metadata file stays authoritative for the descriptor documents, but the manifest attrs still reach the jar and the dev classpath.

Era-correct emission per forge-family loader:

Loader / MC Mixin configs Access transformers forge/lexforge (all) MixinConfigs manifest attr — mods.toml has no [[mixins]] table META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg auto-detected neoforge ≥ 20.3 [[mixins]] in neoforge.mods.toml (better errors) same neoforge < 20.3 MixinConfigs manifest attr same cleanroom / legacy ≤1.12.2 MixinConfigs manifest attr canonical cfg auto-detected; non-canonical outputs additionally listed under FMLAT

Loader-contributed extras merge verbatim: environment.manifestAttributes (env channel — e.g. manifestAttributes["FMLModType"] = "LANGPROVIDER" or ornithe's Calamus-Generation) plus emitter attrs (Fabric-Loader-Version, …). A hand-written src/.../META-INF/MANIFEST.MF folds its attributes into the generated manifest — generated values win on conflict — rather than colliding.

docs.title: Datagen and gametest envs
docs.text:
datagen() / gametest() inside an environment declare auxiliary source sets (<env>Data, <env>Gametest). They inherit the parent's version/mappings and see its classes on their classpath, but emit no metadata of their own — the parent's descriptor references their classes (entrypoints, generated data). A second same-id metadata file would collide on the classpath, so gen<Env>ModMetadata no-ops for aux envs.

Server gametests run through the loader's JUnit artifact (fabric-loader-junit) wired onto testImplementation by gametest(). Client gametests additionally arm the env's automatic <env>Client run with the loader's client-gametest JVM args (fabric: -Dfabric.client.gametest -Dfabric.client.gametest.modid=<project>), so runFabricGametestClient boots the client into the test thread and exits — no manual run-config tweaks needed.

docs.title: Multiple Source Sets & Projects
docs.text:
2.0 rewrite. The 1.x unimined.minecraft(sourceSets.x) API moved — envs live in minecraft { sourceSet(...) { } }; see Migrating from 1.x.

Two shapes cover the 1.x use cases:

  • flat — several sourceSet envs in one project;
  • multi-module — a common module + one subproject per loader (what unimined-cli new --modules generates).

docs.title: Flat: one env per source set
docs.text:
Each minecraft { sourceSet(...) { } } block is an independent environment — its own product, loader, mappings, runs:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")            // env "main"

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        loader("fabric", "0.16.0")            // env "main"

        sourceSet("forge") {
            version.set("1.20.1")
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Sharing between envs
docs.text:
Envs are independent by default; three mechanisms share configuration and classpath:

  • Implicit parent — an env declared inside another env's block (sourceSet("datagen") { datagen() } style nesting, and the datagen/gametest aux verbs) inherits the parent's sections automatically. Opt out with inheritParent.set(false).
  • combineWith(...) — pull another env's declarations in explicitly: combineWith("main"), combineWith("common", env) with sections to take only some (mappings, runs, deps, …).
  • Module deps — modImplementation(project(":common"))-style references share code across projects.

Sibling sourceSet envs at minecraft {} top level don't share — combineWith("main") is the way to layer the main env's config in.

docs.title: Merged: several loaders on one environment
docs.text:
Repeat loader(name, version) inside a single sourceSet env to compile that source set against several loaders' APIs at once — the 2.0 analog of 1.x's merged { fabric; forge }. The first loader(...) is the environment's primary: it owns the production namespace, remapping, metadata emission, and run configs. Every further loader(...) declares a secondary whose product and libraries merge onto the env's compile classpath only — this is not a client/server merge (Side.MERGED is the other axis) and not a packaging merge:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("common") {
            version = "1.20.1"
            loader("fabric", "0.16.0")   // primary — prod/remap/runs
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")    // secondary — compile only
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("common") {
            version.set("1.20.1")
            loader("fabric", "0.16.0")   // primary — prod/remap/runs
            loader("forge", "47.2.0")    // secondary — compile only
        }
    }
}

The env's effective javaVersion floor takes the strictest across all declared loaders. Secondary loaders land on dedicated configurations (mergedLoader<Env> for most loaders, the family-probed forgeMergedLoader<Env> plus fabricMergedLoaderLibraries<Env> for loader-embedded libs) — all compile-only, so common sources see every declared loader's API while production stays per-loader through the normal artifact ladder.

Per-loader envs that need their own runs or outputs compose from the merged env: combineWith("common") (or copyFrom("common", LOADER)) validates by membership — an env may combine from a merged source when its own loader is among the source's declared loaders. Run configs themselves stay per-loader — the merged env's runs launch under the primary; to launch under a secondary, give that loader its own env combining the merged one.
