docs.title: Access declarations in common
docs.text:
A loader-less env applies access files to its own dev artifact the same as a loader env — the apply step is contributed by the shared wiring rather than a loader family, so access { }, from(...) files, and AT/AW/CT files under common/src/main/resources all take effect where common compiles. Downstream envs get the same rules through combineWith: access { } rules re-emit in each child loader's consumed format (AW/CT for fabric, AT for forge), while declared/discovered files propagate through the file collections and merge into each child's canonical doc. Per-file options (from(path) { output }), fileName, and format follow the same propagation — a child's own access { } block wins when it redeclares a name or format.

Dependency-declared access applies to a common env too (loom transitiveAccessWideners parity): modImplementation/ modRuntimeOnly jars are scanned for conventional access docs — *.accesswidener/.classtweaker entries, fabric.mod.json accessWidener/classTweakers refs, META-INF/accesstransformer.cfg + FMLAT manifest entries, and custom.*injected_interfaces keys (synthesized as transitive-inject-interface rules). AW/CT docs apply their transitive-* rules only; ATs apply in full (FML semantics). Headerless dep docs need an unambiguous modSourceNamespaces entry to interpret — skipped with a warning otherwise. Dep jars' embedded access docs are also rebased during their prod→dev remap (remap-access step), matching the loader envs.

A common env's access declarations also ship inside its jar — the architectury.common.json equivalent. The canonical doc emits as a self-describing classTweaker file at <env>-access.classtweaker (access { format = "at" } switches to META-INF/<env>-access_at.cfg, "aw" to .accesswidener, and access { fileName } overrides the whole path), and from(path) { output }/declared files land at their output or a conventional path. Dependents that consume common as a plain dependency — no combineWith — pick these up through the same dep scan: transitive-* rules cross to dependents, the rest stay env-local (loom transitiveAccessWideners semantics). The production remap rebases the embedded doc alongside the jar's other contents, so the published artifact declares it in the production namespace.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
The product is which Minecraft distribution an env runs — orthogonal to the loader. minecraft { } is the native product; others get their own blocks:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    bta { loader("bta-babric", "1.7.6") }       // Better Than Adventure
    reindev { loader("foxloader", "…") }        // ReIndev + FoxLoader
    nsss { file("dist.jar") }                   // Not So Seecret Saturday
    custom("myproduct") { file("custom.jar") }  // arbitrary dist
}

unimined {
    bta { loader("bta-babric", "1.7.6") }       // Better Than Adventure
    reindev { loader("foxloader", "…") }        // ReIndev + FoxLoader
    nsss { file("dist.jar") }                   // Not So Seecret Saturday
    custom("myproduct") { file("custom.jar") }  // arbitrary dist
}

Products nest their loader inside the product env — the loader axis stays the same either way.

Full generated build scripts: BTA / custom product (.gradle siblings are the Groovy twins).

docs.title: Declared-source dists (legacydist)
docs.text:
xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.legacydist is the provider behind envs that declare their game jar directly — legacydist { } selects it implicitly, and custom(...) { file(...) } envs negotiate to it from the declared source. Apply the plugin, then declare the artifact inside the env:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.legacydist")
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            legacydist {
                file("libs/dist.jar")                    // local jar
                // url("https://…", sha256 = "…")         // pinned fetch
                // producer("./gradlew", "buildDist")     // external builder
                namespace = "official"                   // prod namespace
                format = "obf"                           // optional hint
            }
        }
    }
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.legacydist'
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            legacydist {
                file 'libs/dist.jar'
                namespace = 'official'
            }
        }
    }
}

The declared jar is consumed as-is — no manifest is consulted, so it works for non-version artifacts (BTA/ReIndev overlays, pre-1.8 bukkit, air-gapped jars). file() copies into a descriptor-keyed cache under the shared unimined cache; url() downloads once with the SHA-256 pin verified before publish (unpinned URLs warn); maven() resolves from the project's repositories at declaration time; producer() runs the declared executable inside the artifact transform and expects its output in the work dir. format = "obf" marks the jar as obfuscated so it rides the raw→dev remap view; a format matching another registered provider ("devbundle") routes there instead.

docs.title: Paperweight dev bundles
docs.text:
xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.devbundle consumes paperweight-format dev-bundle zips — the data/ + patches/ + config.json layout paperweight uses for paper/folia/custom forks without distribution endpoints (data versions 2–8). Apply the plugin, then declare the bundle on an env with devbundle { } (or legacydist { } with format = "devbundle"):

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.devbundle")
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            devbundle {
                file("myfork-dev-bundle.zip")
                // url("https://example/bundle.zip", sha256 = "…") also works
            }
        }
    }
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.provider.devbundle'
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            devbundle {
                file 'myfork-dev-bundle.zip'
            }
        }
    }
}

The provider extracts the bundle's embedded mojang-mapped paperclip jar and runs it (patch-only) against the vanilla server.jar download, caching everything under the shared unimined cache. The result is an already-patched, mojmap-named server jar — reported with namespaceMode = IDENTITY, so no remap step runs on the dev classpath.

What the bundle maps onto:

  • Artifact — the patched server jar, keyed by side (SERVER/MERGED; CLIENT is rejected — bundles are server-only). completedStages reports paperclip:binpatch.
  • Libraries — the bundle's declared api/compile/runtime coordinates plus the paperclip's own META-INF/libraries.list entries. Maven Central, Mojang Libraries, and Paper's repo are ensured; the bundle's own libraryRepositories are mirrored onto the project.
  • Mappings — server_mappings/client_mappings channels serve the vanilla server-side Mojang map (the bundle's artifact is a server jar, so both keys point there), plus reobf_mappings / access_transformer aux artifacts when the bundle ships them (data versions ≤7 / ≤5 respectively) and paperclip_jar for the extracted tool.

Gaps and edges:

  • producer() declared sources can't run inside the artifact transform — use file()/url().
  • The bundle's source patches/ are not applied — the paperclip output is already patched.
  • launch metadata is absent: Paper servers launch from the patched jar + libraries, not a version-JSON launch profile.
  • custom(name) { provider.set("devbundle"); file(...) } is equivalent for forks that want a custom:<name> product id.

docs.title: Exporting a dev bundle
docs.text:
The same plugin is also the producer: every env gets a devBundleExport spec and an export<Env>DevBundle task that writes a consumable bundle (data version 6) of that env's production artifact:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            devBundleExport {
                apiCoordinates.set("com.example:myfork-api:1.0")
                // serverJar.set(...)        // defaults to the env's
                //                           // minecraftProd view
                // outputZip.set(...)        // defaults to
                //                           // build/devBundle/main-dev-bundle.zip
            }
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    minecraft {
        sourceSet("main") {
            devBundleExport {
                apiCoordinates.set('com.example:myfork-api:1.0')
            }
        }
    }
}

./gradlew exportDevBundle          # main env (export<Env>DevBundle otherwise)
# → build/devBundle/main-dev-bundle.zip — declare it on the consuming
#   side with devbundle { file("…") }

A unimined bundle is a self-contained reproducer: the env's already-built prod jar rides inside data/paperclip-mojang.jar's META-INF/versions/ entries and the paperclip's Main-Class is a generated stand-in that extracts it — consumers get byte-identical output to what the env built, no binary patching involved (so the zip is larger than a patch-based bundle, and exact). patches/ and reobf_mappings carry through for source-level consumers when you supply them (sourcePatches, reobfMappingsFile); the bundle is otherwise deterministic — re-running the task on unchanged inputs produces identical bytes.

What the export maps onto:

  • serverJar — the env's minecraftProd view by default (the prod-namespace artifact through the whole JAR pipeline); point it elsewhere for a custom product.
  • Libraries — the env's minecraft<Env>Libraries deps become META-INF/libraries.list rows and embed physically (META-INF/libraries/) so the bundle launches like a real paperclip; embeddedLibraries.setFrom() empties that for a coords-only slim bundle. libraryRepositories conventions to the project's declared maven repos.
  • Side — dev bundles carry server artifacts; exporting a CLIENT env warns (a deliberate serverJar override may still be right), and a non-mojmap production namespace warns for the same reason.
  • Extras — apiCoordinates/mojangApiCoordinates seed the consumer's compile classpath; bundleId names the bundler version.json/versions.list entry (unimined-<env>-<version>); mainClass writes META-INF/main-class for direct java -jar launch.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
Unimined's publish host (xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish) turns each bound environment's outgoing artifacts into an adhoc component named unimined<Env> (uniminedMain for main). Destination adapters pick those components up; none of them auto-publish components.java.

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined")
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish")
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined'
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish'
}

Auxiliary environments (datagen()/gametest()) are test harnesses — they never produce components or publications.

docs.title: uniminedPublish { }
Maven
docs.text:
One MavenPublication is created per environment component as it binds — uniminedMain → uniminedMain, uniminedFabric → uniminedFabric, etc. Repositories and credentials are plain Gradle publishing {} config:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
publishing {
    repositories {
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.example/releases")
            credentials(PasswordCredentials::class)
        }
    }
}

publishing {
    repositories {
        maven {
            url = uri("https://maven.example/releases")
            credentials(PasswordCredentials)
        }
    }
}

Coordinates default per environment: main publishes as <project.name>; every other environment as <project.name>-<env> (the name-fabric/name-forge convention) — set environment("<env>") { artifactId = ... } to override. Publications that would resolve to identical coordinates fail the build.

Each publication carries the environment's dev and production variants plus sources (Gradle module metadata included): the dev jar rides custom unimined-dev-* usage attributes so plain java-api/java-runtime consumers resolve the production variant unambiguously — request a dev usage explicitly to opt in (see PublishAttributes). publishDev/publishProduction/publishDataFiles on environment("<env>") gate each channel; identity-remap environments publish a single artifact. The loader-merge merged artifact is intentionally not part of the Maven path — it belongs to ModPublisher uploads.

docs.title: In-build production dependencies
docs.text:
Cross-project consumption works the same way inside one build — this is the reobfArtifactConfiguration equivalent. A consumer that needs a sibling project's production jar (e.g. a buildSrc tool or a downstream test module) selects it by attribute on a resolvable configuration or the dependency itself:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
configurations.create("prodTool") {
    attributes {
        attribute(PublishAttributes.CHANNEL, "prod")
        attribute(PublishAttributes.ENVIRONMENT, "fabric")
    }
}
dependencies {
    prodTool(project(":parentmod"))
}

configurations.create("prodTool") {
    attributes {
        attribute(PublishAttributes.CHANNEL, "prod")
        attribute(PublishAttributes.ENVIRONMENT, "fabric")
    }
}
dependencies {
    prodTool project(":parentmod")
}

Plain java-api/java-runtime usage already resolves to the prod variant, so CHANNEL = "prod" is explicit documentation of intent; ENVIRONMENT (and NAMESPACE) disambiguate multi-env producers. The consumable producer configurations are named <sourceSet>Prod{Api,Runtime,Sources}Elements — exposed as PublishConfigurations.prod*ElementsName(sourceSet) for the project(path = ..., configuration = ...) escape hatch. Same-project consumption is just tasks.named("remap<Jar>").

docs.title: Access documents
docs.text:
Each environment also gets an accesstransformer-category variant pair (NeoGradle accessTransformer / ModDevGradle data-file parity): the environment's generated canonical access doc plus every access { from(path) { } }/accessFile(path) { } declaration is published as unimined<Env>AccessTransformerElements artifacts (classified access-transformer[-N]). Dependents pull them by module coordinate instead of scanning the jar:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
dependencies {
    uniminedFabricAccessTransformer("com.example:parentmod:1.0")
}

dependencies {
    uniminedFabricAccessTransformer "com.example:parentmod:1.0"
}

Resolved documents join the environment's dependency access channel — they apply like dep-jar access documents (producer-namespace binding, no transitive- filter, never validated against your mappings) and are not re-shipped inside your own jar. A producer that declares no access documents publishes no variant; when a producer ships several environments' docs, disambiguate with attribute(unimined.environment, "<env>") on the dependency.

docs.title: ModPublisher
docs.text:
xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.publish-modpublisher feeds artifacts and release metadata into com.hypherionmc.modutils:modpublisher's publisher { } as conventions when that plugin is applied (it stays compileOnly — no ModPublisher classes load unless you apply it). There is no adapter DSL — publisher { } is the single surface for what can't be inferred, and anything you set there wins:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
publisher {
    apiKeys {
        curseforge(providers.environmentVariable("CURSE_TOKEN").get())
        modrinth(providers.environmentVariable("MODRINTH_TOKEN").get())
    }
    curseID.set("1234")
    modrinthID.set("abc")
    versionType.set("release")
    debug.set(true)   // dry-run: builds the upload plan, uploads nothing
}

publisher {
    apiKeys {
        curseforge(providers.environmentVariable("CURSE_TOKEN").get())
        modrinth(providers.environmentVariable("MODRINTH_TOKEN").get())
    }
    curseID.set("1234")
    modrinthID.set("abc")
    versionType.set("release")
    debug.set(true)   // dry-run: builds the upload plan, uploads nothing
}

Conventions supplied automatically: artifact (the forgix mergedElements jar when adapter-forgix is applied, else the first bound env's production jar — remap<Env>Jar when it remaps, else jar), additionalFiles (remaining per-loader prod jars), loaders (bound envs' loader names), gameVersions (env versions), and version (project.version). The merged artifact suppresses the per-loader jars; aux envs are excluded; dev artifacts are never uploadable.

docs.title: Manual verification (live upload)
docs.text:
Automated coverage (ProjectBuilder dry-run tests) asserts the config lands on publisher { } — it does not upload. Verifying a real release still needs a human pass:

  • [ ] publishMod with debug.set(true) and a real merged jar — inspect the dry-run plan (files, version, loaders, gameVersions).
  • [ ] Real upload to a staging/draft Modrinth or CurseForge project with scoped tokens via env vars — confirm version, changelog, loaders, game versions, and additional files on the platform UI.
  • [ ] Confirm API keys come from providers only (never literals in the build file) and never appear in logs.

docs.title: Loader-jar merging (forgix)
docs.text:
The adapter-forgix adapter (plugin id xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix) merges per-loader production jars with Forgix's engine:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
plugins {
    id("xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix") version "..."
}

plugins {
    id 'xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.adapter-forgix' version '...'
}

Every bound environment's production jar feeds mergeLoaderJars automatically (remap<Env>Jar, or jar for non-remapping envs; auxiliary environments are excluded), keyed by loader name — most multi-loader builds need no configuration. Forgix's own plugin isn't required (its DSL only supports multi-project layouts); when applied, its forgix { } merge configurations feed in too, and loaderMerge.from(...) adds or overrides any input. The merged jar is published on the consumable mergedElements configuration (classifier merged) — the ModPublisher adapter prefers it as the upload artifact and suppresses the per-loader jars when it exists. See adapters/forgix.

docs.title: Remap Pipeline
docs.text:
unimined { remap { } } configures the remapping steps — the verbs are ordered pipeline steps applied to the MC jar and remapped mod deps:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    remap {
        unpick("path/to.unpick")
        applyClassTweaker { /* custom bytecode transform */ }
        sourceRemap { /* UML source remapper — the default engine */ }
        jst { /* explicit opt-in: Java Source Transform */ }
    }
}

unimined {
    remap {
        unpick("path/to.unpick")
        applyClassTweaker { /* custom bytecode transform */ }
        sourceRemap { /* UML source remapper — the default engine */ }
        jst { /* explicit opt-in: Java Source Transform */ }
    }
}

Source remapping runs through UML's source remapper by default; jst { } remains as an explicit engine opt-in for verification or alternate-engine use.

docs.title: Mod artifacts
docs.text:
After the namespace remap step, JAR-surface pipelines automatically run a modArtifacts step that rewrites mod-jar metadata the base remap leaves untouched:

  • kotlin.Metadata internal names (any Kotlin mod jar)
  • mixin configs and refmap emission for jars carrying *.mixins.json
  • JarModAgent/ClassTransform refmaps for jars whose manifest declares JarModAgent-Refmaps

The step is engine-agnostic — it applies identically when remap is overridden with remap("tiny"), and to remapped dependency views, so mod deps get mixin refmaps for the dev runtime. Declare it explicitly with jar { modArtifacts() } only to pin an engine or ordering; it is skipped on identity remaps and on jars without the relevant resources.

docs.title: Standalone artifact remapping
docs.text:
unimined:remap works outside a Minecraft environment — any jar can be remapped between namespaces with remap.artifact(...), which registers a remap<Name>Artifact task:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
uniminedRemap {
    artifact("baritone") {
        input.set(layout.projectDirectory.file("baritone.jar"))
        mappings.set(layout.projectDirectory.file("mapping.txt"))
        from.set("target")   // optional — see autodetection below
        to.set("source")
        // output defaults to build/remapped/baritone-remapped.jar
    }
}
// ./gradlew remapBaritoneArtifact

uniminedRemap {
    artifact("baritone") {
        input.set(layout.projectDirectory.file("baritone.jar"))
        mappings.set(layout.projectDirectory.file("mapping.txt"))
        from.set("target")   // optional — see autodetection below
        to.set("source")
        // output defaults to build/remapped/baritone-remapped.jar
    }
}
// ./gradlew remapBaritoneArtifact

The mapping file is autodetected from its contents at execution time — no format flag is needed:

Format Notes SerializedMappingData bundle Native unimined zip; richest payload (multiple views) MappingBundle JSON Legacy unimined row bundle tiny v1 / v2 Fabric-era standard UMF Unimined Mapping Library universal format SRG / CSRG / package SRG Forge-era formats TSRG v1 / v2 Forge-era formats ProGuard / RetroGuard Common for shipped obfuscated jars (e.g. Baritone) MCP / mcpconfig MCP exports — v1/v3/v6 method+field CSVs, mcpconfig zips Parchment Javadoc/param overlay — must be named parchment.json to autodetect

ProGuard maps are the common case for third-party obfuscated jars (e.g. remapping a shipped mod to readable names). Sidecar formats (AW/AT/CT, nest, exception, signature, unpick) also parse via UML but carry no class-name columns, so they are not useful as a standalone mappings input.

When from/to are unset, namespaces are autodetected from the input jar: the namespace column whose class names best match the jar's contents becomes from, and the single remaining column becomes to. Autodetection fails with an actionable error when no column matches or more than one target candidate remains — set both explicitly in that case.

The step pipeline is shared with the environment machinery — remap { jar { } } declarations apply to artifact tasks too (engine selection via remap("tiny"), access steps, custom steps). Environment-scoped steps and modArtifacts are not applied; those only make sense on environment jars.

docs.title: Production-jar validation (footgunChecks)
docs.text:
After the pipeline, remap<JarTask> (and remap<Name>Artifact) stamps the manifest with Unimined-Mapping-Namespace: <target> — a remapped jar is self-describing — then lints the emitted artifact for packaging mistakes that compile fine but fail at runtime:

  • metadata files parse (fabric.mod.json, quilt.mod.json, mcmod.info, META-INF/mods.toml, META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml, plugin.yml/bungee.yml/paper-plugin.yml, *.mixins.json) and carry their required keys
  • every path the metadata references exists inside the jar: accessWidener files, declared mixin configs, jars[] nested jars, icon files
  • classes named by metadata exist: fabric entrypoints, mixin classes listed in *.mixins.json, the plugin.yml main class
  • the manifest namespace marker is present and matches the target namespace

Findings default to ERROR — the task fails. The level is a remap-block property:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    remap {
        footgunChecks.set(FootgunCheckLevel.WARN) // log and continue; OFF disables
    }
}

unimined {
    remap {
        footgunChecks.set(FootgunCheckLevel.WARN) // log and continue; OFF disables
    }
}

Sources jars get the marker but skip metadata/class checks (a sources jar legitimately lacks .class files). Only unimined-produced artifacts are linted — third-party jars in transforms are never validated.

docs.title: Scripting surface
docs.text:
The pipeline is data, not code — specs serialize at transform registration — but three escape hatches cover scripting needs:

  • applyClassTweaker { ... } (and the other apply* verbs shown above) attach a custom bytecode transform to a surface without writing a step type.
  • step(spec) / step(MySpec::class.java) { ... } append any StepSpec to a surface. Engine plugins expose their own verbs by registering them via RemapExtension.registerDslVerb(name, factory) — this is what makes jst {}, unpick {} etc. reachable from Groovy (methodMissing dispatch), where Kotlin extension functions would be invisible.
  • uniminedTools { ... } overrides the resolved coordinates of external tool jars the pipeline shells out to (jst, unprotect, mcpcleanup, diffpatch, stitch, forgix, classpathPluginLoader, jvmdowngraderJavaApi) — see Adapters.

The resolved pipeline is inspectable lazily: uniminedRemap.stepSpecs(envName, RemapSurface.MINECRAFT) returns a Provider<List<StepSpec>> — useful for diagnostics or wiring downstream tasks off the effective step list without re-resolving mappings.

docs.title: Run Configs
docs.text: runs { } is top-level. Every environment gets auto-registered run configurations, each materializing a run<Name> task plus IDE run configurations from genIdeRuns.

docs.title: Auto-registered runs
docs.text:
Environment Runs main client, server, prodClient, prodServer <env> <env>Client, <env>Server, <env>ProdClient, <env>ProdServer datagen envs the env's own name (e.g. data → runData) gametest envs <env>Client/<env>Server plus test-task wiring

Forge-family loaders (forge, lexforge, neoforge, cleanroom) also declare the userdev run types — data, clientData, serverData, gameTestServer, junit — which materialize as runData, runGameTestServer, … (<env>Data on non-main envs) with no runs.create needed. A run type the resolved profile doesn't declare launches the plain environment launch.

The prod* variants launch against minecraftProd — Minecraft in the namespace shipped mod jars are remapped to — with your remapJar output and direct (un-remapped) mod dependencies: the shipped-runtime check (1.x runObfClient/runObfServer parity). FG2-era forge is the exception: real production launches the shipped obf jar and lets FMLDeobfTweaker remap obf→searge at runtime, so prodClient/prodServer there resolve minecraftRaw plus the runtime-deobf flags instead of the pre-deobfed artifact.

docs.title: Reaching runs
RunConfig fields
docs.text: Field Purpose environment which env's classpath/dirs the run launches (convention: the env it was registered for) enabled false = the run<Name> task exists but fails with a "disabled" message — gate runs on env/CI conditions beforeRun(task) / beforeRun { } task deps/actions wired ahead of launch (e.g. build a datapack first) side CLIENT/SERVER — defaults from the run name type loader run-config key (runs.<type> in forge userdev profiles) — defaults to the run name; set type.set("data") on a renamed run to bind the data launch shape prod true = production-namespace MC artifact + remapped jar mainClass launch main class (loader-provided by default) jvmArgs / programArgs launch arguments javaagents file collection rendered as -javaagent: flags (unimined agents attach here — jarmod, expectplatform, CPL) environmentVariables process env systemProperties -D JVM system properties — typed alternative to raw jvmArgs -D strings; rendered ahead of jvmArgs so an explicit -D there still wins launchProperties / setProperty(k, v) ${key} substitution values applied to args/jvmArgs/env at launch — setProperty("user", "Dev") then programArgs.add("--username=\${user}"). Lazy forms: Provider, () -> String, and a Groovy closure; user keys win over env defaults and loader keys logLevel / loggingConfigFile root log level for a generated log4j2 dev config (-Dlog4j.configurationFile is added automatically), or an explicit config file that overrides it additionalRuntimeClasspath per-run classpath additions — files appended to this run's launch only; maven coords go on the run<Name>Dependencies configuration stdin piped into the launched process features version-json rule features (is_demo_user, has_custom_resolution) width/height --width/--height args downloadAssets fetch assets before launching (default true) username offline-name shorthand bridging into auth.username auth { } typed session spec — see Auth ideName / ideFolderName IDE run-configuration display/file name (defaults to the run name) and an optional folder/group label ideConfigGenerated false suppresses this run's IDE run-configuration emission — genIdeRuns skips it singleInstance true marks the emitted IntelliJ configuration "single instance only" (singleton="true" — IDEA refuses a second concurrent launch); IDEA emitter only, no effect on run<Name> execution unitTest marks the run as a JUnit test run — a Gradle Test task (test<Name>) materializes alongside run<Name>; conventions to true for junit-typed runs on forge-family loaders (gametestJunit capability). The loader's program args ride an args-file in fml.junit.argsfile, jvm args an @argfile unitTestSources source sets supplying test classes + classpath for a unitTest run — defaults to test loadedMods which of the environment's mods { "<id>" { } } groups this run loads — loadedMods("a", "b") selects a subset; empty (default) loads all declared groups. Selected groups join the launch classpath and serialize into the loader's mod-grouping channel (fabric.classPathGroups / MOD_CLASSES)

docs.title: Argument substitution
docs.text: Loader capability templates and your own args support ${...} launch-property substitution (game_directory, auth_*, classpath, …) plus {modid} — resolved against mod { id } at run time (e.g. fabric gametest's -Dfabric.client.gametest.modid={modid}). Declare your own keys with setProperty — they resolve lazily at launch and override the built-in/loader-supplied values for that run.

docs.title: Dev-time manifest attributes
docs.text:
Dev runs launch exploded output dirs, not a jar — but FML (modern SecureJar and legacy CoreModManager) parses META-INF/MANIFEST.MF inside classpath directories, so manifest attrs still apply. gen<Env>ModMetadata writes the emitted manifest body into generated resources (build/generated/unimined/mod/<env>), which the source set packs into the resources output — runClient/runServer classify the env's output with FMLModType, MixinConfigs, FMLAT, TweakClass, … exactly like the built jar. To test a non-MOD classification in dev, set mod { loader("forge") { fmlModType("LANGPROVIDER") } } — the attribute reaches both the dev classpath and the shipped jar from one declaration.

Loader dev-mode flags are wired per-loader: fabric-family runs get -Dloader.development=true/fabric.development (and quilt's loader.development) from the env wiring — no run-config edits needed. Anything else is ordinary jvmArgs/environmentVariables.

docs.title: Dry-run
docs.text:
-Punimined.run.dryRun prints the assembled launch (main class, args, classpath) instead of exec'ing — the quickest way to inspect what a run would do:

./gradlew runClient -Punimined.run.dryRun

docs.title: Launch scripts
docs.text:
genLaunchScript<Name> resolves the same launch as run<Name> but writes runnable run<Name>.sh / run<Name>.cmd into the run's working directory (run/<env>-<name>/) instead of exec'ing — for launching outside Gradle, e.g. under a debugger or another terminal. genLaunchScripts (plural) emits them for every declared run:

./gradlew genLaunchScriptClient
# or everything:
./gradlew genLaunchScripts
./run/main-client/runClient.sh

The scripts cd into their own directory, export the launch environment, and exec java with the fully resolved args/classpath — the same values run<Name> would use.

docs.title: Listing runs
docs.text:
uniminedRuns prints one line per declared run config (task, env, side, type, prod flag, enabled, main class) — a quick check of what runs { } materialized:

./gradlew uniminedRuns

docs.title: Cache maintenance
docs.text: pruneUniminedCache prunes the global unimined cache (~/.gradle/caches/unimined), deleting entries idle longer than 30 days by default — --age-days 0 removes everything, --project additionally wipes the project's .gradle/unimined, --assets includes the shared assets dir.

docs.title: IDE integration
docs.text: genIdeRuns emits per-env IntelliJ .idea run XML and Eclipse .launch files for every declared run — regenerate after editing runs { }.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: See Auth — auth { microsoft() } per run or runs { auth { } } as the default; :loginMicrosoft populates the credential store; unimined.auth.* properties control storage.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
xyz.wagyourtail.unimined.source wires genSources / gen<Env>Sources per bound environment. The default pipeline for an environment with no provider-supplied sources:

  1. Decompile — the env's dev-namespace Minecraft artifact through the selected engine (vineflower by default). Inputs are the jar, classpath, and engine options, so up-to-date checks skip reruns (@DisableCachingByDefault — no build-cache entry).
  2. Sources-surface steps — the env's RemapSurface.SOURCES pipeline (e.g. uml:remap renaming the decompiled .java to the dev namespace) runs over the decompiled jar when steps are declared.
  3. Linemapped classifier — gen<Env>Linemapped applies the vineflower 0x4646 linemap extras to the binary jar's LineNumberTables, producing -linemapped.jar whose stack traces and debugger line mappings track the decompiled/enriched source lines.

bsm=1 (bytecode source mapping — the linemap extras) is on by default; engine options can override it:

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    source {
        engine.set("vineflower")
        options.put("bsm", "1")
    }
}

unimined {
    source {
        engine.set("vineflower")
        options.put("bsm", "1")
    }
}

Artifacts land in the env's generated local-repo as minecraft-<env>-<version>-sources.jar and -linemapped.jar.

docs.title: External decompiler engine
docs.text:
engine.set("external") runs any fernflower-CLI-compatible decompiler jar — selected by coordinate via generator(dep) (a bare version string is shorthand for org.vineflower:vineflower:<version>):

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    source {
        generator("org.vineflower:vineflower:1.10.1")
        // or pin a different decompiler entirely:
        // generator("org.quiltmc:quiltflower:1.9.0")
    }
}

unimined {
    source {
        generator("org.vineflower:vineflower:1.10.1")
    }
}

docs.title: Fork options
docs.text: jvmArgs (default -Xmx4G -Xms1G -Xss4M) sizes the forked decompiler JVM; javaVersion (default 17, empty string disables) selects the toolchain it runs on; args (default -jrt=1) appends raw CLI arguments after the -key=value engine options.

docs.title: Provider-supplied sources
docs.text: When the product provider ships a devSources artifact (e.g. Forge userdev's mcpconfig chain), the decompile step is skipped entirely — the supplied sources remap straight to the dev namespace.

docs.title: Mod sources
docs.text:
Three distinct "mod sources" flows exist — they answer different questions:

  • Your own sources for publishing — the env's remap<SourcesJar> output rides the *ProdSourcesElements variant of the unimined<Env> component, so a published -sources classifier carries the production namespace (see Publishing).
  • Dependencies' published -sources jars — the <bucket>SourcesRemapped views below remap each dep's shipped sources artifact into the dev namespace for IDE attach.
  • Dependencies without shipped sources — genModSources / gen<Env>ModSources decompiles the env's modImplementation / modRuntimeOnly dependencies (already remapped to the dev namespace) through the same engine + RemapSurface.SOURCES pipeline as genSources, then publishes each result under the dep's own coordinates in the env's generated local repo. The dep set is resolution-time and unbounded, so the decompile runs as an artifact transform chained off the remapped mod views — the task just resolves the views and writes the repo entries.

docs.title: Dependency -sources attach
docs.text:
Every bound environment also gets per-bucket views over the mod dependencies' published sources jars, complementing genModSources for deps that ship -sources at all (no decompile, no repo publish — the remapped file materializes at resolution like any transform output):

  • <bucket>SourcesRemapped requests each dep's docs variant (category=documentation, docsType=sources — maven's -sources.jar or a withSourcesJar-style sourcesElements variant) and runs it through the environment's RemapSurface.SOURCES pipeline, mod source namespace → dev namespace, so IDE-attached sources carry dev names.
  • <bucket>SourcesDirect is the identity-environment pass-through twin; consumers pick by isIdentityRemap exactly like the *Direct/*Remapped jar views.

The active remapped views are registered on MinecraftExtension.modDevSourcesViewConfigurations under "<environmentId>:<bucket>" keys (the sources counterpart of modDevViewConfigurations). Because the dep source namespace is the declared one — modSourceNamespaces, like the jar views — a sources jar published in another namespace remaps wrongly.

Consumers resolve leniently and filtered to module/project component ids: deps that ship no -sources artifact contribute nothing, and file deps must be excluded or they would contribute their own jar as "sources".

docs.title: Decompiler cleanup on mod sources
docs.text:
Fernflower-era decompilers emit raw numeric arguments for OpenGL calls — GL11.glBegin(7) instead of GL11.glBegin(GL11.GL_QUADS). Each bound environment gets an opt-in cleanupSources / cleanup<Env>Sources task that rewrites those literals to the named GLxx/ARB* constants using the same gl_constants.json dataset RetroFuturaGradle ships (applyDecompilerCleanupToMain parity):

./gradlew cleanupSources        # main environment's source set
./gradlew cleanupServerSources  # the 'server' environment

The task walks the environment's bound source set's java.srcDirs and modifies matching .java files in place — run it once after pasting decompiled code into your mod, not as part of the normal build. Only files importing org.lwjgl.opengl. are touched, only changed files are written (atomically), and constant-owning classes the rewrite references (e.g. ARBVertexBufferObject) get their imports inserted automatically. Generated/patched source dirs the environment injects under build/ are excluded — the task is for your checked-in sources.

docs.title: Transform
docs.text:
unimined { transform { } } is the environment-transform surface the transform-* modules plug into — each loader module (forge, fabric, jarmod, bukkit, …) registers its pipeline here, and you can hang project-local steps on the same hooks.

unimined {
    transform {
        // every environment
        transformer(MyTransformer())

        // one environment's source-set spec
        sourceSet("main") {
            transformer(EnvOnlyTransformer())
            decorator(LogOutputDecorator())
        }

        // run-time transform behaviour for a specific run config
        transformRun("client") { /* ... */ }
    }
}

Per environment (sourceSet("<env>") { }):

Knob Purpose transformer(t) append a MinecraftTransformer to the env's jar pipeline decorator(d) append a TransformDecorator (log/observe the pipeline) nestedJars { } jar-in-jar packaging — see Dependencies features { } feature flags the env's pipeline consults

Transformer execution is lazy: each registered transformer becomes a Gradle task in the env's chain (prod-<jarTask> → remap<JarTask>), with inputs wired through providers so the pipeline stays configuration-cache safe.

Most projects never touch this — loaders wire their own transforms (patch apply, userdev pipeline, jar merge) and mod packaging lives in Mod Metadata + remap { } steps (Remap Pipeline).

docs.title: Migrate
docs.text:
unimined { migrate { } } registers migrateMappings — the loom migrateMappings equivalent: rewrite your sources onto a different mappings release (or a different mapping family) in one pass.

Kotlin build.gradle.ktsGroovy build.gradle 
unimined {
    migrate {
        migrateMappings("main") {
            target {
                yarn("1.20.2", 2)      // any mappings {} verb works here
            }
        }
    }
}

unimined {
    migrate {
        migrateMappings("main") {
            target {
                yarn("1.20.2", 2)
            }
        }
    }
}

Then:

./gradlew migrateMappings          # main env
./gradlew migrateFabricMappings    # a non-main env (migrateMappings<Foo> still runs as a deprecated alias)

Migrated sources land in remappedSrc/ — outside src/ so they can't become an accidental source root. Non-code files copy verbatim; rewrites are reported per file and unmapped references come out as warnings, not failures.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The task grafts your environment's resolved mapping tree onto the target tree through a shared namespace, producing a direct devNamespace -> target mapping, then runs a source remapper over allSource. The bridge namespace is picked in order:

  1. bridgeNamespace.set("...") if you set it
  2. the env's production (modSourceNamespaces) namespaces
  3. intermediary, then official
  4. any other namespace the two trees share

If the trees share nothing it fails listing the candidates — pick compatible mappings or set bridgeNamespace explicitly. The target column is auto-detected (named/mojmap/yarn/mcp, else last); override with targetDevNamespace when the target carries several.

docs.title: Task knobs
docs.text:
Knob Purpose target { } target mappings — the full mappings { } DSL (yarn(...), mcp(...), maven(...), builtin(...), file(...), …) classpath("g:a:v") extra artifacts on the remapper classpath — e.g. the new-version intermediary jar for cross-MC-version migrations bridgeNamespace explicit graft bridge when auto-detection can't find a shared namespace targetDevNamespace which target column becomes the new sources' namespace outputDir default remappedSrc/

Typical flows: yarn→newer-yarn across MC versions (bridge: intermediary, add classpath("net.fabricmc:intermediary:<newMc>")), dev-named → mojmap (bridge: official), and MCP/SRG-era upgrades (bridge: searge).

The result is a source rewrite — after diffing remappedSrc/ into src/, update mappings { } to match the target you migrated to.

docs.title: DSL Index
docs.text:
The 2.0 DSL surface, by extension:

Block Where Purpose unimined { } root top-level plugin extension minecraft { } unimined env bound to a source set (native product) bta/reindev/nsss/custom(n) unimined product envs loader(n, v) env apply a modloader mappings { } env remap chain mod { } unimined mod metadata (id/depends/loader()/mixins) runs { } root run configurations remap { } unimined remap pipeline steps transform { } unimined transform hooks migrate { } unimined migration helpers loaderApi(n, v) unimined loader api coordinates loaderApiModule(n, m, v) unimined one api sub-module modImplementation & co dependencies remapped mod deps (env-scoped)

docs.text:
The KDoc/Javadoc API reference is generated with Dokka when the docs are deployed.

Open the API reference

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: unimined new <name> / unimined init — generate a modding environment for any MC version.

docs.title: Getting the CLI
docs.text:
Each release ships two runnable builds — pick by platform:

Artifact Run unimined-cli.kexe (GitHub release asset) ./unimined-cli.kexe new mymod — self-contained Linux x64 native binary unimined-cli-node.zip (GH release asset) unzip, node unimined-cli.js new mymod — needs Node.js

On other platforms, build the JVM fat jar from source: ./gradlew :unimined-cli:fatJar → java -jar unimined-cli/build/libs/unimined-cli-fat.jar new mymod.

new <name>  — generate a project in ./<name>
init        — generate in the current directory
Flag Meaning --group base package group --version/--mc MC/product version --plugin-version unimined version to apply --loader <name=v> repeat = multiloader; v empty = registry default --product <p> bta, reindev, nsss, custom:<name> --modules common + per-loader subproject layout --dist <path> dist artifact for custom:/nsss — path, maven:<coord>, or url:<url> --mappings "<dsl>" mappings chain lines --var k=v mappings-scope variables --side <side> client, server, merged --jarmod JarModAgent transforms (modloadermp shape) --jars split|merged MC jar shape for jarmod-era envs --modid/--package/--mod-version mod identity (--mod-version defaults 1.0.0) --metadata dsl emit mod { } metadata block --extra "<line>" raw build.gradle.kts lines --no-wrapper skip gradle-wrapper download --include-build <path> composite pluginManagement resolution --toolchain <n> pin the java toolchain --dsl kotlin|groovy emitted DSL flavor --templates <zip> / --template <name> extract a bundled project zip --out <dir> output directory --gradle <version> Gradle wrapper version to pin --offline skip version probes — disk cache + baked versions only --no-version-props inline literal versions instead of gradle.properties keys

docs.title: Generation modes
docs.text:
Exactly one layout per project — the CLI picks it from the flag combination:

Mode Trigger Emitted structure FLAT default One module; all envs in a single unimined { minecraft { } } block MULTILOADER --modules common subproject + one subproject per --loader, env per subproject CUSTOM_PRODUCT --product <p> One module; a non-native product env — bta { }/reindev { }/nsss { }/custom("<name>") { } per --product template extraction --templates <zip> (+ optional --template <name>) testing/<name>/ extracted wholesale from a unimined-templates zip — scaffold flags ignored

Era modifiers compose with the layout modes:

Modifier Effect --jarmod client/server source sets, clientJar/serverJar tasks stamping JarModAgent-Transforms, <modid>-<side>.transform stubs --jars split per-side MC jar tasks (jarmod-era; merged = one jar) --side client|server single-side env instead of merged
